title: Senior Engineering Manager, Product Engineering
description:
Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zone

Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.

At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.

I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.

Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.

That means a strong engineering manager who can still ship. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You won't ship weekly — you'll need focus — but you'll build with the team often enough to know the playbook still works.

You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.

— Grigory

Why Secfix exists

Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.

Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.

We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.

This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.

What you'll actually do in the first 3 months

This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes:

Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. You don't need to be the fastest engineer in the room, but the team needs to see that you can build at the level you'll ask of them and can ask the right questions.

Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start regular 1:1s with each engineer, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI.

Month 3: Own hiring. Take over engineering interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews.

What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months?

After the first quarter, the job is management and the technical decisions. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — most of that hiring is yours to run.

You won't ship weekly, but you'll build something with the team now and then, because that's how you know the playbook still gets things out the door. Our CS and Sales leaders work the same way — they still own a small slice of the IC work, so they have skin in the game.

Here's what you'll be close to in the next months:

- Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it.

- Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20.

- Team and hiring. Team structure, growth conversations, the hiring process, and eventually the next manager.

- AI in the craft — and in the management. Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff.

What success looks like

At 6 months: The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality. Our agentic engineering playbook is noticeably better because of you — you’ve added or rewritten the skills, rules, and AI review checks the team uses every day, and you lead by example in how you ship with agents.

At 12 months: The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've found and/or coached the EM Nr. 2 to support growth.

How we work

We've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture.

- Focus is sacred. Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our thoughtful communication and our remote culture ; give it a read.

To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year:

- Small, temporary teams. A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution.

- AI is already part of the craft. We use Claude for product design exploration and spec drafting. Engineers work in Cursor with encoded skills and rules that live in the codebase — component patterns, folder structure, architecture choices, and the path from Figma to Angular code. AI checks code against architecture rules before human review. We have a dedicated design QA skill that compares Figma against coded output. We don't use AI to lower the bar; we use it to reach the bar faster with more iterations behind us. In case you’re interested, we wrote a piece about it here .

- Zero-bugs. We take this seriously - this helps us to gain customer trust faster. Especially serious customer-facing problems don't sit in a backlog competing with roadmap work. title: Delivery Manager - Generation Flex
description:
Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

Kraken Generation Flex
The energy industry is undergoing the largest transformation since industrialisation at an unprecedented rate of change and we are positioning ourselves to be at the heart of that change.

Our aim is to be the leading global provider of solutions that enable customers to release £30bn of value per annum from distributed energy resources (DERs). We are building a Software as a Service (SaaS) subscription business with a global addressable market of £2.4 billion per annum, by digitally connecting hundreds of thousands of DERs with energy markets.

We have already attained a market leading position and Kraken is a recognised thought leader and innovator in the industry.

🏠 Where you'll fit in: 

As we enter a stage of rapid commercialisation and growth, we're looking for a Generation Flex Delivery Manager to own the successful onboarding of flexible generation and energy assets onto KrakenFlex across the EU with a focus on Germany.

This is a customer-facing delivery role with a strong technical bias. You'll manage an asset through the full onboarding journey, from initial discovery and technical analysis, through site design and gateway installation, to commissioning, testing and handover into live service.

You'll sit at the intersection of our customers, Electrical Engineering, Product and Customer Success Engineering teams. You'll need to understand both the connectivity and control architecture of our customers' assets and how those assets connect to and operate through the KrakenFlex SaaS platform .

You won't be expected to design the details of the integration solution or write the software yourself. Instead, you'll need enough technical depth across both areas to understand how they fit together, identify gaps and risks, challenge incomplete information and drive the right conversations to get a site successfully integrated.

Your role is to bring together three perspectives throughout onboarding:

Customer : What is the customer trying to achieve, and what do we need from them?

Product : How will the asset operate within KrakenFlex, and what product capabilities and configuration are required?

Engineering : How does the physical asset need to be integrated, connected and commissioned to make that solution work?

Your job is to make sure those three come together as one successfully delivered customer solution .

🚀 What you'll own: 

- Own the end-to-end onboarding and delivery of Generation Flex assets BESS (grid-scale and C&I) and RES (Wind and Solar), from initial onboarding through analysis, site design, installation, configuration, commissioning, testing and handover into live service.

- Build a strong understanding of the Generation Flex product and SaaS platform , including how assets are represented, configured, monitored and controlled within KrakenFlex.

- Understand how the physical site and its electrical/control systems connect into the KrakenFlex software architecture, and bring those two worlds together throughout onboarding.

- Work closely with Product and Software Engineering teams to understand the relevant GenFlex capabilities, product modules, configuration requirements and technical constraints for each customer and asset.

- Translate between customer requirements, electrical engineering requirements and SaaS/product requirements , making sure each group understands what is needed from the others.

- Understand the end-to-end data and control path from the physical asset through site controls, meters, PPCs, gateways and communications infrastructure into Kraken Flex, and from Kraken Flex back to the asset where control is required.

- Ensure that the customer's intended use of the GenFlex product is reflected in the technical onboarding solution, including the required telemetry, controls, configuration, integrations and product modules.

- Be able to explain to customers how their site will interact with KrakenFlex, both from a physical integration perspective and from a software/product perspective.

- Work with Product teams to identify where customer or asset requirements do not fit current product capabilities, and ensure gaps, constraints or product dependencies are surfaced early.

- Feed recurring onboarding challenges, customer requirements and technical integration pain points back into Product and Engineering teams to help improve and scale the GenFlex proposition.

- Be the primary delivery point of contact for customers during site onboarding, setting clear expectations around what we need from them, what Kraken is delivering and what needs to happen next.

- Work closely with our Electrical Engineering and Customer Success Engineering teams to ensure the technical information required to integrate a site is complete, accurate and available at the right stage of delivery.

- Review and interpret customer technical documentation including:

- Electrical Single Line Diagrams (SLDs)

- Network and communications diagrams

- Site and asset specifications

- PPC and controller documentation

- Modbus register maps

- IP addressing and network information

- Functional Design Specifications

- Metering and telemetry information

- Hardware and connectivity requirements

- Be confident discussing technical site architecture with customers and engineers, understanding how equipment such as generators, batteries, meters, PPCs, controllers, gateways and site networks fit together.

- Identify missing, inconsistent or technically unclear customer information early and drive it to resolution before it becomes a delivery blocker.

- Coordinate the preparation and review of Kraken integration documentation, including gateway architecture, communications diagrams, Kraken SLDs, integration designs and site configuration information.

- Coordinate the Kraken Gateway delivery and installation process , ensuring prerequisites such as power, networking, connectivity and installation arrangements are understood and ready.

- Manage readiness for key commissioning and testing activities, including:

- Gateway installation and connectivity

- Operational acceptance testing

- Kraken market and service testing

- Proactively manage delivery risks and communicate issues and mitigation plans clearly to internal and external stakeholders.

- Surface blockers early and drive the right people together to resolve them rather than allowing issues to sit between teams.

- Maintain clear visibility of the status and health of each site, including technical readiness, product readiness, customer actions, Kraken actions and upcoming milestones.

- Continuously improve the Generation Flex onboarding process, identifying recurring technical, product or customer blockers and working with Engineering, Product and Operations teams to remove them.

🧠 What you'll bring to the party: 

- A strong technical background and the confidence to work closely with electrical, control systems, and networking.

- A practical understanding of industrial networking and communications , including concepts such as IP addressing, LANs, routers, switches, VPNs and site connectivity.

- Enough electrical engineering knowledge to understand concepts such as metering, breakers, transformers, generators, inverters, batteries and asset control systems.

- Experience delivering technical projects involving the integration, commissioning or onboarding of physical assets, ideally within energy, renewables, utilities, industrial automation, controls or a similar environment.

- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to take a complicated technical problem and clearly explain the issue, impact, owner and next action.

- Experience coordinating multiple teams and dependencies across customers, Electrical Engineering, hardware, installation partners and other third parties.

- A highly organised approach to delivery, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple sites at different stages of onboarding simultaneously.

- The ability to proactively identify risk, remove blockers and maintain momentum in an environment where customer readiness and site timelines can change quickly.

- A customer-centric mindset and a drive to provide an outstanding onboarding experience without compromising technical quality.

- A pragmatic, collaborative approach and the confidence to operate in a fast-moving environment where processes and products are still evolving.

- A strong interest in understanding how a SaaS product works end-to-end , rather than treating the software platform as a black box.

- A drive to get things done in a collaborative, agile environment , comfortable navigating the complexity and comfortable being the regional face of site onboarding function.

- Language: professional fluency in German and English 

⭐ Bonus points 

- Experience in APIs, data flows, system integrations or cloud software architecture would be beneficial.

- Experience in flexible generation, battery storage, renewable energy, demand response or distributed energy resources.

- A working understanding of industrial communication protocols and controlled environments would be helpful (e.g. modbus, OPC UA

- Experience commissioning or integrating generators, BESS, solar, EV infrastructure or other industrial energy assets.

- Previous experience working with grid-connected assets, control systems or energy market services.

- Experience with SaaS implementation, technical product onboarding or systems integration.

- Familiarity with commissioning processes and the distinction between cold commissioning, energisation and hot commissioning.

- Experience with industrial gateways, edge devices or IoT connectivity.

title: Senior B2B Sales Manager
description:
YOUR FUTURE, ON DEMAND 

The ideal blend of stability and flexibility. A genuinely human employer that cares for people and the planet. True autonomy to shape what comes next, for us and you. This is the perfect platform to take your career where you want. 

Back in 2005, we pioneered Europe’s first TV streaming service. Today, we're a leading TV streaming provider with millions of monthly users, and since 2021 we've been ClimatePartner-certified. Over 200 colleagues of 47 nationalities. We’re the grown-up start-up, helping to shape a better future since day one. That hasn’t changed, even if the world has. We’re friendly, international, inclusive – and our people say we’re reliable and transparent, too. It’s why they trust us and believe in what we do.

THE ROLE 

Make Zattoo the TV platform partner of choice for operators and broadcasters in Eastern and Northern Europe. This role turns new markets into lasting revenue and shapes Zattoo’s next stage of growth. You will join a close-knit team working across Germany and Switzerland that values trust, collaboration and hands-on ownership over hierarchy and heavy process.

THE TEAM 

The Zattoo Business Sales Team is responsible for all sales activities related to Zattoo’s TV-as-a-Service and streaming technology offerings, including the End-to-End TV platform as well as Modular products such as Streaming, Ingest and Orchestration solutions. We work closely with Product, Portfolio Management, Marketing, Client Success and Project Management to bring complex solutions to market and build long-term customer relationships across different regions and customer segments.

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

- Build a new business pipeline across Eastern and Northern Europe and win telcos, ISPs, broadcasters and OTT platforms as long-term customers

- Own complex, high-value deals end-to-end, from first conversation to signed contract

- Navigate long decision cycles and orchestrate our Sales Engineering, Product and Legal teams to get deals over the line

- Build lasting relationships with senior decision makers up to C-level

- Shape tailored offers from our modular platform (INGEST, STREAM, ORCHESTRATE, E2E)

- Be Zattoo’s face in your markets, at customer meetings, trade shows and partner events, and bring market insights back to Product

WHAT YOU’LL BRING 

Experience required (Must-have) 

- 10+ years in B2B enterprise sales, closing complex deals with long sales cycles

- Proven track record selling to telcos, broadcasters, media companies or platform providers

- Deep understanding of the TV, OTT and streaming market

- Established network in Eastern and/or Northern European markets

- Confident negotiating with C-level and procurement teams

- Business fluent English

Nice to have 

- Language skills in one or more Eastern or Northern European languages

- Experience selling modular tech or SaaS platforms

- German language skills are advantageous

Behavioural Competencies 

- Ownership: Takes full responsibility for their markets and deals, without relying on a large sales support machine.

- Honest Forecasting: Reports pipeline and forecast realistically and transparently, including bad news early.

- Team Player: Works closely with Product, Sales Engineering and Legal and values collaboration over individual heroics.

- Hands-on Mentality: Comfortable building structures and materials themselves where needed.

- Long-term Thinking: Builds relationships for the long run instead of chasing quick wins.

WHY JOIN US? 

At Zattoo, you’re always on firm ground with real freedom to explore. You’ll have the support and opportunity you need to go far, while you’re helping us create a sustainable and entertainment-filled future for all. 

WHAT WE OFFER YOU 

- Reward : strong market competitive salary

- Recharge : 30 days vacation plus public holidays

- Regulate : trust based flexible working hours and the option for remote work worldwide for up to 8 weeks per year 

Plus: 

- We’re sharing: Free access to the best streaming experience on the market

- We're developing: Your own development budget, German classes and Zattoo all-company hack days

- We’re inclusive: ‘ Zattooies’ are a fun, engaged, and diverse team made up of 47 nationalities

- We’re healthy: Health checks, mental wellbeing support, team sports and more!

- We’re mobile: Discounted BVG tickets and free bike rentals

- We’re sociable: A calendar of events with fireside chats, lunches, in-house bar, BBQ’s, monthly socials, summer party and an annual off-site event

Zattoo enables our users to view indiscriminately and we reflect that in our team too. Regardless of race, gender, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, disability or any other characteristic protected by law we encourage everyone to apply and will give everyone equal consideration. We are an equal opportunities employer — join us and help build a diverse team dedicated to revolutionising the way you watch TV.

We are committed to ensuring fair, open, and equitable hiring practices and are happy to answer any questions you may have about us or the role throughout the whole process. In line with the EU Pay Transparency Directive, we share the applicable compensation range with you before your first interview.

title: Forward Deployed Engineering Manager
description:
As the Forward Deployed Engineering Manager, you will lead the team that puts Auterion's robotic systems to work with customers in the field. We build complete systems: vehicles, sensors, onboard compute, radio links, autonomy software, and ground control. Your job is to understand how all of it fits together and to make it work in real missions.

You will lead your team through the entire customer engagement, from discovery and integration to field trials and handover. You are not a hardware specialist. You are a systems engineer who can trace a problem across every layer of the system, lead people well, and earn the trust of demanding customers.

Responsibilities and Duties 

- Team Leadership & Mentorship: Lead and grow a cross-functional team of Forward Deployed Engineers covering systems integration and software. Hire, coach, and develop your engineers. Build a culture of ownership and proactive problem-solving.

- Accountability: Keep the bar high for yourself and your team. Work directly with stakeholders across the company. You will have a close relationship with the CTO, CEO, VP of Engineering, and the engineering directors.

- Field Deployment Oversight: Own technical delivery of customer deployments in demanding, non-standard environments. This covers system configuration, connectivity, mission readiness, and operation under environmental constraints.

- System Integration: Act as the technical lead for high-stakes customer integrations. Ensure the full system works end to end: vehicle, payloads, onboard compute, communication links, autonomy software, and ground control.

- Field Troubleshooting: Diagnose failures across hardware, firmware, software, and communications. Use logs, telemetry, and structured debugging to find root causes fast.

- Stakeholder Management: Serve as the primary technical contact for defense and enterprise customers. Translate operational requirements into deployment plans that account for system performance, link quality, power, and mission constraints. Run technical meetings, demos, and field days.

- Feedback Loop & Release Coordination: Work closely with Product and R&D to feed field results and real-world edge cases back into the product. Coordinate with R&D on platform releases so customer deployments stay current and stable.

Qualifications and Skills 

- Systems Engineering: 7+ years in technical roles in robotics, drones, autonomous vehicles, or comparable complex embedded systems. You understand the full system end to end and how a change in one subsystem affects the others.

- Leadership Experience: 3+ years managing a technical, customer-facing team (Field Engineers, Forward Deployed Engineers, Solutions Architects, or similar). You have dealt with underperformance and built team culture deliberately.

- Software Skills: Comfortable working in Linux. You write Python, read C++, and use Git. You debug from logs and telemetry, not only at the bench.

- Hardware Fluency: You understand hardware at integration level: power, sensors, interfaces, and RF basics. You do not need to be a hardware designer.

- Field Deployment Expertise: Hands-on experience with field-deployed systems where "turning it off and on again" isn't always an option. Understanding of networking and radio communication is a major plus.

- Crisis Management: Proven ability to troubleshoot critical failures in the field under high pressure and with limited physical access to the hardware.

- Customer Presence: Composure and credibility in front of demanding customers. You communicate clearly with engineers and decision-makers alike.

- Languages: Fluent English. German is a strong plus.

- Work Authorization: Must hold EU citizenship and be eligible to work in the European Union without restriction.

Nice to Have 

- Experience with PX4, ArduPilot, or ROS2

- Background in defense or government programs

- Eligibility for German security clearance

Benefits 

- Flexible working hours

- Stock Options

- Generous holiday allowance

- Pension plan 

- Extended social security package 

- Enhanced maternity & paternity leave

- Wellpass membership 

About Auterion 

We are building the leading software platform for AI-powered autonomous systems for enterprise and government customers. Our team is supporting the most important missions and solving the most challenging problems.

At Auterion, we bring together the sharpest minds who love to solve the hardest problems. Join a vibrant team built on innovation, openness, and excellence, where you’ll be empowered to develop ideas, collaborate across all levels, and make an impact that matters.

title: Operations Intern - Renewable Supply
description:
Operations Intern - Renewable Supply 

Festanstellung, Vollzeit · Berlin (HQ)

Unsere Mission für dich 

Gestalte mit uns die nachhaltige Energieversorgung von morgen und werde Teil unseres wachsenden Operations-Teams! trawa baut Europas führende B2B-Plattform für saubere Energie auf. Unsere Mission ist es, Industriekunden mit nachhaltigen Energielösungen zu versorgen. Mit einem innovativen Ansatz, der Energieversorgung, fortschrittliche Energiemanagementsoftware und intelligente Optimierung von Energieverbrauchsdiensten kombiniert, helfen wir Unternehmen dabei, erfolgreich zu bleiben und den Weg in eine klimafreundliche Energiezukunft zu ebnen.

Das Team 

Du wirst Teil eines kleinen, eingespielten Onboarding-Teams mit vier Personen. Als Teil des Business Operations Departments arbeitest du in einem Bereich mit insgesamt rund 20 Kolleginnen und Kollegen, zu dem auch das Customer Success Team gehört. Im Alltag verbindet uns eine enge, cross-funktionale Zusammenarbeit, mit der wir gemeinsam die bestmöglichen Ergebnisse für unsere Kunden erzielen. Wir unterstützen uns gegenseitig, denken mit und packen gemeinsam an. Gleichzeitig pflegen wir eine Teamkultur, die über den Arbeitsalltag hinausgeht – und eine Company Culture, auf die wir wirklich stolz sind.

Als Operations Intern (m/w/d) spielst du eine Schlüsselrolle im Aufbau von Prozessen und Strukturen eines aufstrebenden und schnell wachsenden Technologie-Startups. Wir stellen fortlaufend für eine Praktikumsdauer von 3–6 Monaten ein.

Deine Aufgaben 

- Ownership für operative Prozesse: Du führst entscheidende operative Aufgaben in Eigenverantwortung durch und trägst dazu bei, dass unsere Organisation in allen Kernbereichen reibungslos läuft.

- Automatisierung von Prozessen: Du entwickelst Ansätze zur Effizienzsteigerung und Automatisierung von Prozessschritten.

- Begleitung beim Onboarding: Du unterstützt bei der Einführung unserer Neukund:innen in das trawa-Universum und sorgst für eine exzellente Kundenerfahrung.

- Beitrag zur Weiterentwicklung der Organisation: Du gestaltest Prozesse aktiv mit und hilfst uns dabei, als Unternehmen weiter wachsen zu können.

- Daten im Blick behalten: Du übernimmst die Datenpflege in unseren Systemen (z. B. CRM) und stellst durch sorgfältige Arbeit eine hohe Datenqualität sicher.

Nach wem wir suchen 

- Du bist Student:in, im Bachelor-Studium, Gap Year, Master-Studium oder Absolvent:in mit guten akademischen Leistungen.

- Erste praktische Erfahrungen in Startups, anderen schnelllebigen Umfeldern oder der Energiewirtschaft sind ein starkes Plus.

- Du denkst analytisch, fühlst dich wohl im Analysieren von Zahlen und kommunizierst datenbasierte Erkenntnisse sicher.

- Organisationstalent zeichnet dich aus – du arbeitest strukturiert, behältst den Überblick und kannst Aufgaben effizient priorisieren.

- Du besitzt eine generelle Affinität für digitale Tools wie z. B. CRM-Systeme, Notion, Google Workspace oder n8n.

Deine ersten 90 Tage: 

Die ersten sechs Wochen – Orientierung und Einarbeitung

- Lerne unsere Prozesse kennen – vom internen Handover der Neukunden von Sales, über die Anmeldung von Lieferstellen bis hin zur Marktkommunikation im komplexen Energiemarkt.

- Mache dich mit den wichtigsten Tools, Systemen sowie internen und externen Ansprechpartnern vertraut, die beim Onboarding unserer Neukunden eine Rolle spielen.

- Führe deine ersten Kunden-Onboardings eigenständig durch: Stelle die „Handover-Readiness" durch Sales sicher, richte das Kundenportal ein, initiiere den Kundenkontakt, melde Lieferstellen an und löse Probleme in der Marktkommunikation.

Bis zum dritten Monat – Verantwortung übernehmen und Prozesse weiterentwickeln

- Übernimm Kunden-Onboardings eigenständig und verantworte Timelines sowie die Kommunikation mit allen Beteiligten.

- Entwickle ein belastbares Verständnis für Marktkommunikationsprozesse und werde zur verlässlichen Ansprechperson bei Problemen in deinem Bereich.

- Erkenne wiederkehrende Muster in typischen Fehlern und bring eigene Ideen ein, um unsere Onboarding-Prozesse gezielt zu verbessern.

Warum wir? 

Gestalte mit uns die Zukunft der Energiewirtschaft und treibe eigenverantwortlich Projekte voran, die echten Einfluss haben – auf unsere Produkte, unsere Kundinnen und Kunden und die Umwelt. Das erwartet dich bei uns:

- Dein Impact: Du übernimmst Verantwortung in unserem dynamischen Team und gestaltest aktiv innovative Produkte, die die Energiewende vorantreiben und zur Dekarbonisierung des Mittelstandes beitragen.

- Flexibles Arbeiten: In unserem schönen Office fördern wir eine lebendige Unternehmenskultur. Homeoffice ist ebenfalls eine Option. Mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten, 30 Urlaubstagen und 10 Tagen Workation unterstützen wir deine Work-Life-Balance.

- Attraktive Benefits: Neben einem wettbewerbsfähigen Gehalt erhältst du Essensgutscheine, eine Urban Sports-Mitgliedschaft, reichlich kostenlose Snacks und ein persönliches Produktivitätsbudget.

- Persönliche Entwicklung: Du bist Teil eines tollen Teams, wo Coaching und Mentoring groß geschrieben wird, und arbeitest mit Spitzentechnologien und lernst von Branchenexpert:innen.

- Vielfalt & Inklusion: Bei uns sind alle willkommen – wir engagieren uns für einen integrativen Arbeitsplatz, der Vielfalt wertschätzt. Wir ermutigen Menschen unterschiedlichen Geschlechts, Alters, sexueller Orientierung, ethnischer Zugehörigkeit, sozialer Herkunft und körperlicher oder neurodiverser Vielfalt zur Bewerbung.

Über uns 

Willkommen im trawa-Universum! Wir haben es uns zur Aufgabe gemacht, das grüne Versorgungsunternehmen der Zukunft von Grund auf aufzubauen. Wir schaffen einen direkten Zugang zu erneuerbarer Energie für B2B-Industrieunternehmen, entwickeln Software und Technologie, um die Volatilität des Energiemarktes zu bewältigen, und professionalisieren die Energiebeschaffung auf der Käuferseite.

title: Machine Learning Engineer (f/m/d)
description:
Focused Energy is building the future of clean energy through laser-driven inertial fusion. Backed by our $240M Series A — the largest fully secured Series A in the global fusion industry — we are scaling rapidly across multiple geographies.

Based in Germany and the US, we have brought together the top scientific and engineering minds using proven technologies to unlock fusion power at commercial scale. Focused Energy is working to realize game-changing scientific innovation that promises to deliver a clean, sustainable and abundant source of power globally.

Your Role 

This role sits at the intersection of ML engineering and computational physics, working within our Software Engineering & Digital Twin environments. You'll collaborate closely with optical engineers, laser and fusion physicists, simulation scientists, and systems engineers to embed data-driven intelligence directly into our Digital Twin architecture. You’ll be reducing design risk, shortening development timelines, and unlocking system-level optimization that purely physics-based approaches can't achieve at the speed we need.

You will design, build, and deploy machine learning models that enhance, accelerate, and augment our multiphysics simulation environments across our high-energy laser systems, target injection and tracking system, target manufacturing system, and fusion chamber. This will enable faster design cycles, predictive system optimization, and real-time decision support across our laser, targetry, and fusion programs.

What You'll Do 

- Surrogate & reduced-order modeling: Design and deploy surrogate and reduced-order models (ROMs) that replace or accelerate high-fidelity multiphysics simulations in the Digital Twin environment

- Physics-informed ML: Develop physics-informed machine learning (PIML) and physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) that embed physical constraints (Maxwell's equations, thermodynamics, fluid dynamics) directly into model architectures

- ML pipelines: Build and maintain ML pipelines for training, validation, uncertainty quantification (UQ), and continuous model refinement against experimental and simulation data

- Active learning & Bayesian optimization: Implement active learning and Bayesian optimization workflows to intelligently guide design space exploration and reduce costly simulation runs

- Digital Twin integration: Integrate trained ML models into the broader Digital Twin framework, interfacing with HPC simulation outputs (COMSOL, ANSYS, custom solvers) and real-time sensor data

- Anomaly detection: Develop anomaly detection and predictive diagnostics models to monitor system health and identify off-nominal behavior in laser subsystems

- Autonomous optimization: Apply reinforcement learning and Bayesian control approaches to support autonomous or semi-autonomous optimization of laser operating parameters

- Cross-functional collaboration: Collaborate with Digital Twin architects, systems engineers, and optical simulation scientists to ensure ML models meet fidelity, latency, and uncertainty requirements

- Engineering rigor: Establish best practices for model versioning, reproducibility, testing, and documentation in a fast-moving research environment

Who You Are 

Must-Haves 

- Master's or PhD in Machine Learning, Computational Physics, Applied Mathematics, Data Science, Computer Science, or a closely related field

- Proven experience building, training, and deploying ML models for complex physical systems; strong command of deep learning (PyTorch, TensorFlow/JAX), probabilistic models, and uncertainty quantification

- Expert-level Python; proficiency in C++ or Fortran a plus; experience with HPC environments (batch schedulers, MPI/OpenMP parallelization)

- Fluency working with PDE-based simulation outputs, time-series sensor data, and high-dimensional parameter spaces typical of multiphysics environments

- Hands-on experience with Gaussian processes, neural network surrogates, reduced-order models, or equivalent metamodeling techniques

- Experience building robust ML pipelines for scientific data — including preprocessing, feature engineering, model validation, and deployment

- Ability to communicate model behavior, confidence intervals, and limitations clearly to physicists, engineers, and non-ML specialists

- Strong cross-functional team skills; comfort working in an interdisciplinary environment spanning physics, engineering, and software

Nice-to-Haves 

- Experience with physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) or neural operators (DeepONet, FNO) applied to physical systems

- Background in laser physics, plasma physics, high-energy-density science, or related complex physics domains

- Experience with digital twin platforms and live integration of ML models with simulation environments (e.g., NVIDIA Omniverse, Siemens Xcelerator, ANSYS Twin Builder)

- Familiarity with multidisciplinary design optimization (MDO) workflows, including Design of Experiments (DoE), sensitivity analysis, and uncertainty propagation

- Experience applying reinforcement learning to physical system control or optimization

- Familiarity with Monte Carlo methods and statistical uncertainty quantification frameworks

- Experience with MLOps tooling (MLflow, Weights & Biases, DVC) in a scientific computing context

- Interest in fusion energy, advanced laser systems, or high-energy-density physics

title: Senior/Staff Platform Engineer - Rust (d/f/m)
description:
🤓 About Luminovo

At Luminovo , we’re building the infrastructure that turns the electronics supply chain into something software can read and act on. Our customers use it to quote PCBAs faster, find cost savings and act on risks in their supply chain.

We serve 300+ customers, from Europe’s largest EMS to category-leading OEMs, with around 100 Luminerds across Munich, Berlin, New York and Austin. We’re backed by Chalfen Ventures, Cherry Ventures and General Catalyst. With data centers and robotics driving demand for electronics, someone needs to manage that supply chain, and they’ll need good software to do it. ( Here’s why we care so much about electronics .)

🚀 Your role

Team Core is our platform team. Its job is to make all our other engineering teams more productive and to improve our codebase and infrastructure as a whole. You’ll:

- Keep our DevOps setup and CI/CD pipelines fast and reliable

- Build tools every team needs (e.g. interface for building permissions)

- Act as an in-house Rust expert: our backend is a Rust monolith, and Team Core helps the other teams use good Rust patterns and architecture

- Be responsible for the Developer Experience (DX).

- Help our engineers use agents more productively

Other details 

- Location: remote-first, within two hours of CET. We prefer Munich > Berlin > Germany > Europe.

- Tech stack: Rust, TypeScript + React, Postgres, Clickhouse, Redis, Kafka, Kubernetes, Helm, Flux

- 🇺🇸 Some of the work in this role falls under US export control regulations (ITAR), so you must be a US citizen . You’ll need to be based in Europe, and if you’re currently in the US, we’ll support your relocation to Germany.

🖲️ Our tech stack 

We always try to use the best tools available for the job. Don't worry, we don't need you to be familiar with all of these:

- Main monolith is written in Rust (using actix-web as our web framework), deployed on Kubernetes

- React and Typescript for frontend

- PostgreSQL for persisting our data

- Redis for caching and queues

- Flux for GitOps

- Honeycomb, Prometheus and Grafana for monitoring and observability

- garden-io for developing on Kubernetes

- Azure and Cloudflare for cloud computing

🤓 Whom you’ll be working with 

- Timon , one of our Founders

- Alex and Tomas , two of our Staff Engineers

- Inga , Senior Software Engineer

⚡️ Skills, knowledge, and expertise

Just so you know – we purposefully did not create a standard list of minimum qualifications for this role. We care much more about your motivation and ability to help us accelerate technical progress than we care just about your CV. If you're interested to find out more about why we banned requirements from our performance profiles – see here .

⚡️ About Luminovo 

Luminovo is the first electronics supply chain platform that unites all data, processes, and stakeholders in the trillion-dollar electronics industry . 

We fundamentally believe that technology is the best tool that humankind has developed to tackle the biggest challenges we face as a society today. And we want to do our share in accelerating technological progress. 

We bring innovations to life faster and cheaper by creating a more connected and resilient electronics supply chain. 

To date, over 300 active customers worldwide are working with us towards this shared goal. Supported by leading investors such as Cherry Ventures, General Catalyst/LaFamiglia, Chalfen Ventures, and others, we have raised more than €20 million .

Our core principles: putting people first & building great things 

As a remote-first company headquartered in Munich, our brilliant team is spread across cities including Munich, New York, Austin, Calgary, Berlin, London, Valencia, Nairobi, and Verona, among others. 🌍

Our team includes a mix of product enthusiasts, people advocates, business masterminds, and engineering experts. Among us are graduates from institutions like Stanford University and the University of Cambridge, as well as talented individuals with unconventional CVs. What matters most is their drive to build great things.

We provide an authentic environment based on psychological safety to empower Luminerds from various backgrounds to succeed, grow, and focus on impact. Putting people first means that we deeply care about who our employees are, what makes them unique, and what they excel at.

title: Principal Product & Brand Designer (m/f/x)
description:
Build something that truly matters 

At Cortea , we envision a world where every audit is proactively managed by humans and AI agents collaboratively . Where auditing professionals have superhuman capabilities at their fingertips to strengthen the trust in the world's most critical systems.

We're not just improving auditing workflows, we're redefining how audits are done from the ground up. With a rapidly growing, global customer base and backing from world-class investors, the market is ready. What we ship next decides how big this gets.

This is your chance to join a team of sharp, ambitious and kind builders extremely early. Shape the company at its pivotal moment and build something that truly matters .

About the role 

At Cortea, design earns trust, and we sell to an industry that exists to produce it. Auditors are paid to be skeptical, and people judge quality by what they can see: the product, the website, the deck a partner opens in a boardroom, the newsletter someone reads with their first coffee. All of it is Cortea.

This is a role for someone with great taste in designing software and AI systems. You'll find novel patterns for problems that haven't existed in software before, and you'll own how Cortea looks and feels to the outside world.

Roughly 70% product, 30% brand . The product work is deep, expert-facing and systems-heavy. As we are doubling down on design, you'll be working on taking the core flows to the next level. The brand work is yours to own outright: website, marketing and sales visuals, newsletter, event and content assets. It'll be on screen in a Big4 boardroom, in every customer's inbox, and on the wall at the events we host. A lot of surface for one designer, and all of it yours.

We're not looking for someone to ask whether the logo goes left or right. We're looking for someone with opinions.

What you'll do 

- Work directly with our founders, engineers, and customers to turn audit flows into intuitive, delightful interfaces

- Work with Jonas on product design and design strategy overall

- Own our brand designs and visuals

- Evolve our visual identity and design system

- Take increasing ownership of brand direction. Website, marketing and sales material, content and event assets

- Help shape the product vision, roadmap, and user experience standards

- Run usability tests, build user feedback loops, and bring a systems mindset to design decisions

You'll be great at this if you 

- Have product design experience in B2B / SaaS , ideally in fast-moving startups.

- Think in experiences, not screens. With taste you can defend. Product and brand are one surface; you can explain why details work, and you call out when they don’t.

- Want to create a unique brand, which auditors love . Identify, marketing, web should be a draw, not a tax. Taste and passion matter more than volume.

- Can hold complexity without losing clarity. You turn configuration-heavy, expert workflows into clear systems.

- Use AI without sacrificing quality. You've worked out which parts of the job benefit from automation and which need your judgment.

- Work well in ambiguity. You take rough direction and deliver great work without handholding.

- Have low ego. Best idea wins. You give and take feedback without making it about you.

Titles are fuzzy. If you're operating at principal level, or you're currently freelancing and curious rather than actively looking, talk to us anyway.

What you will get 

- Full brand ownership, shape how the product feels . Work face-to-face with experienced founders and learn directly from customer insights.

- Real influence on strategy . In a small team of excellent engineers and operators with high autonomy, you will shape product direction. Best idea wins, regardless of seniority.

- Fast, ambitious, and fun team . Decisions get made in hours, not weeks. Rapid experimentation is the default.

- Meaningful equity and competitive salary . You are one of the first to build this, and you share in the upside.

- A mission that matters. Building intelligent systems for a $200bn industry from Berlin, with AI at the core

I nterview process 

- First Call — Intro on what we do with Liza 

- Second Call — Portfolio walkthrough with Jonas 

- Third Call — Get to know our product and culture with our Co-Founder Valentin 

- On-site Day — Meet our full team in our Berlin office and work on a real problem together with us.

title: Senior Technical Product Manager - Compliance & Recording
description:
About Us 

1GLOBAL is a technology-driven global mobile communications provider helping enterprises and consumer brands deliver seamless connectivity worldwide. Powered by a best-in-class telecom platform, proprietary eSIM technology, and its own mobile core network across 15 countries, 1GLOBAL operates as a fully regulated telecommunications provider in 43 countries.

Founded in 2022, 1GLOBAL has rapidly become one of Europe's fastest-growing telecom technology companies, connecting more than 80 million people and devices globally. Our customers include leading banks, multinational enterprises, global retailers, travel companies, payment service providers, and digital-first businesses.

Headquartered in the Netherlands, with R&D hubs in Lisbon, Berlin, and São Paulo, 1GLOBAL employs over 550 professionals across 16 countries. With annual revenues exceeding US$200 million and a strong track record of profitability, we continue to invest in innovation, infrastructure, and international expansion as we redefine the future of global mobile connectivity.

About the Team 

The Compliance & Recording team owns 1GLOBAL's products for regulated enterprises. We capture mobile voice, SMS and data at network level, with no app on the device, and deliver it to wherever our customers need it: their own on-site recorders and archives, or our Cloud Compliance service built on Verint Financial Compliance. On top of the recordings we offer Communications Analytics, which brings AI transcription, summaries and risk insights to compliance teams.

Our customers include 8 of the world's 10 largest banks. They rely on us for a complete, auditable record of every regulated call and message, so reliability and precision are at the heart of everything the team builds. We work closely with engineering, network, security, service delivery and commercial teams.

We are looking for a Senior Technical Product Manager to own how recorded communications are captured, delivered and analysed. This is an API-first, backend role: there is little UI at its core, because for our customers the integration is the product.

About the Role 

You will lead product strategy and delivery for Compliance & Recording, from the APIs and delivery channels that move recorded data into customer environments to the AI capabilities we build on top of it. 

- Own the vision, roadmap and backlog for Compliance & Recording, covering customer-managed (on-site) recording, Cloud Compliance and the integrations that connect them to customer systems.
- Define and evolve how recorded voice, SMS and data reach customers through APIs, SFTP, SMTP and S3 bucket pushes, choosing the right mechanism for each use case.
- Write precise technical requirements: API contracts, payload and metadata schemas, delivery guarantees, retry and failure handling, security controls and acceptance criteria.
- Lead large projects for our biggest compliance customers, onboarding their engineering and compliance teams with proper documentation, from scoping through rollout.
- Define and track success metrics such as delivery success rate, latency, capture completeness and time to integrate, and keep the roadmap aligned with regulatory change and the competitive landscape.
Requirements 

About You

description:

About the Team 

The Enterprise team owns 1GLOBAL's products for businesses: global mobile connectivity for multinational enterprises, delivered through one platform, one contract and one invoice. Our customers manage their entire mobile estate in the Enterprise Portal, from subscriptions, usage and invoices to orders such as SIM swaps and suspensions, spend alerts, user roles and single sign-on.

We recently retired two legacy portals and moved every enterprise customer onto our new Enterprise Portal. That has created strong demand and a steady flow of requests from customers and internal teams, with a lot of exciting work ahead. We work closely with engineering, design, customer support, customer success, account management, operations and commercial teams.

We are looking for a Product Manager to shape the next chapter of the Enterprise Portal: what we show, how we show it, which reports and analytics we offer, and which actions customers can take themselves. This is a UI and UX-heavy role, where design judgement matters as much as sharp prioritisation.

You will lead discovery and delivery for the Enterprise Portal, turning a high volume of customer and internal requests into a clear roadmap and a portal that enterprise customers enjoy using.

title: UX Research Intern
description:
About baesh

baesh is a social platform connecting people in real life through events, communities, and shared interests.

We’re a small team using AI to move quickly from ideas to working experiences. Research is central to how we decide what to build and whether it’s good enough to ship. Your work will help us stay close to people as the technology moves faster.

You’ll work closely with our Head of Product and UX , an experienced researcher with a PhD in emotional and behavioural research. You’ll get practical guidance across the research process—from deciding what to investigate to helping the team act on what we learn.

This is an unpaid mandatory internship for students whose university programme requires a placement.

- Location: Mostly remote, with opportunities to join research and events in Berlin.

- Start date: Flexible, depending on your university requirements.

- Duration: As required by your university, usually 3–6 months.

What you’ll help with

Usability testing and idea validation

- Help plan and run usability tests on our app and prototypes, including interfaces built with AI.

- Explore how easily people can discover events, join communities, and create their profiles.

- Test whether experiences make sense to real people, beyond looking polished or functioning technically.

- Validate early ideas and assumptions before the team invests further.

- Identify confusing moments and recommend improvements that make a meaningful difference.

Exploratory research and interviews

- Help interview existing users and people who haven’t tried baesh yet.

- Explore how people make friends, find things to do, and connect with communities.

- Understand their needs, motivations, habits, and barriers.

- Help write discussion guides and ask open questions that uncover useful insights.

- Bring people’s experiences into product decisions, keeping the human connection at the heart of how we build.

AI-supported research

- Use AI to help draft interview guides, usability-testing scripts, and survey questions.

- Explore how AI can support research synthesis by organising notes, summarising sessions, and suggesting patterns.

- Check AI-generated summaries and interpretations against what participants actually said and did.

- Learn where AI saves time, where it misses nuance, and where your judgement matters most.

- Help us develop practical ways to combine faster research workflows with thoughtful, reliable findings.

Recruitment and ongoing feedback

- Help recruit participants and coordinate research sessions.

- Support Friends of BAESH , our community of early adopters who contribute through interviews, user testing, feedback, and feature suggestions.

- Help create short in-app surveys about specific parts of the experience.

Making sense of what we learn

- Analyse feedback and identify patterns across sessions.

- Turn findings into clear insights and practical recommendations.

- Share research with the product and development team to shape what happens next.

- Help organise our research so we can build on previous learning.

You won’t be expected to do all of this independently from day one. We’ll guide you, give you feedback, and gradually help you take ownership of research activities.

What you’ll bring

- You’re enrolled in a degree programme that requires a mandatory internship.

- An interest in UX research, psychology, human–computer interaction, design, sociology, or a related field.

- Curiosity about people and a willingness to question assumptions.

- Good listening skills and an empathetic, respectful approach.

- Strong communication skills in English.

- An organised approach and willingness to take initiative.

- An interest in using AI thoughtfully, including questioning its output.

Preferred, but not required: 

- German-speaking , so you can support research with German-speaking participants.

- Some familiarity with interviews, usability testing, surveys, or qualitative analysis—university projects count.

- Experience experimenting with AI tools for research, writing, analysis, or prototyping.

- An interest in social products, communities, and how digital experiences support real-life connections.

You don’t need previous professional UX research experience. We’re looking for curiosity, care, and a willingness to learn.

What you’ll gain

- Research mentorship: Learn directly from an experienced UX and behavioural researcher.

- Practical experience: Contribute to exploratory interviews, usability testing, surveys, and idea validation.

- Experience with AI-enabled product development: Learn how to assess and improve products when building is fast and informed judgement matters more than ever.

- Visible impact: See your findings shape the experiences we build and release.

- Portfolio experience: Develop research case studies, with guidance on what can be shared.

- Flexible working: Agree a schedule that fits your university’s placement requirements.

- A small, collaborative team: Work closely with the people designing and building the product.

Interested?

If you have relevant university work or a portfolio, we’d love to see it—but it’s optional.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Inference Performance
description:
About Tensordyne 

AI is transforming our world. It can perform cognitive functions that previously only humans could do, such as perceiving interactions across different modalities and environments - with the ability to quickly learn and then solve complex problems. Tensordyne is an AI system solution company that builds very high-performance, low-power generative AI inference systems. Our mission, through the creation of custom silicon, hardware and software, is to enable multimodal Generative AI inference acceleration at scale, with safe, sustainable, high-performance systems for our hyperscaler and neocloud data center customers. We are at the leading edge of advancing the latest research and product improvements for generative Al inference solutions that will make Al even more advantageous for compelling new generative AI applications.Tensordyne is a well funded, fast-paced startup company with headquarters in both Sunnyvale, CA, and Munich, Germany. We also have many talented team members working remotely across North America and Europe. We take care of our people and their families with comprehensive benefits, competitive compensation, flexible spending options, and recognition programs, because building category-defining technology starts with a healthy, supported team. Come join us as we shape the future of multimodal generative artificial intelligence!

The role

You'll build the software stack that takes a model from code down to the hardware: the abstractions, kernels, libraries, and tools that engineers and agents use to reach peak performance. Help optimize the latest AI models on our silicon.

Our hardware is designed to be straightforward to program, so the goal is not to hide it. The goal is to expose the right level of control at each layer, from our compiler-driven Python SDK to our low-level Rust programming stack, and to make every performance gap measurable and every fix permanent.

We're looking for a builder who understands hardware deeply and develops with agents by default. You'll own substantial parts of one of these layers and work closely with engineers across models, compilers, runtime, and hardware. Your focus is performance: where cycles, bandwidth, and communication go, and how to win them back. Number formats and model accuracy are owned by our conversion and emulation team; you'll partner with them where precision and speed meet.

What you'll do

- Build the stack. Design APIs, kernel abstractions, and libraries in our Python SDK or Rust stack so model engineers and agents can reach high performance at the layer that fits their problem.

- Make models fast. Take priority workloads, from LLMs to multimodal models, to peak performance on real silicon. Profile, find the bottleneck across kernels, compiler, runtime, and parallelism, and fix it at the right layer.

- Close the gap between model and measurement. Compare measured performance against analytical models and simulation. Explain every material gap, and turn the explanation into a fix or a better model.

- Build the agentic performance loop. Give agents the profilers, traces, counters, and benchmark harnesses to form a hypothesis, change code, and measure the result in minutes. Make the results trustworthy enough to act on.

- Set the bar for performance. Define how we measure, track regressions, and report results.

- Build for the next chip. Design abstractions that carry forward to future hardware generations. Work with hardware architects to test how architectural choices affect real workloads.

What we need from you

- You understand hardware performance. You've optimized AI workloads on GPUs or custom accelerators and can reason about compute utilization, memory hierarchy, latency hiding, synchronization, and multi-chip scaling.

- You build excellent software. You've owned substantial systems from design through production. You're strong in Python and/or at least one systems language such as Rust, C++, or C, and rigorous about interfaces, abstractions, and testing. We care about engineering quality more than a specific language.

- You understand LLM inference end to end. You can read a new model's implementation and reason about prefill, decode, attention variants, KV caches, MoE, and parallelism, and how they map to compute, memory, and communication.

- You build with agents. Agentic development is how you work, not an experiment. You'd rather build the loop that finds the optimization than find it by hand, and you know when the loop still needs a human.

- You build things others succeed with. You've designed APIs, libraries, or performance tooling that other engineers adopted.

- You drive problems to resolution. You form clear hypotheses, measure, and follow the evidence across software and hardware boundaries. You take ownership of the result.

If you hit a few of those boxes, we'd like to speak to you.

We'd be thrilled if you had

- Experience with embedded, bare-metal, or low-level runtime programming.

- Experience with MLIR, other compiler frameworks, or kernel DSLs such as Triton, Pallas, NKI, or CuTe.

- Contributions to LLM serving stacks such as vLLM or SGLang, or a track record of taking end-to-end inference workloads to competitive performance on a hardware target.

Why join us

Your code will decide how fast models run on our hardware, and how easy it is for the next engineer, or the next agent, to make them faster. You'll own a layer of a new programming model, work directly with the people designing the hardware, and see your decisions tested on real silicon and carried into the next generation.

The role

You join the team that finds, evaluates, finances and integrates the tax firms that join Taxforce. You work directly with our founders on live deals and own your workstreams from first screening to closing and beyond.

Tasks

- Deal sourcing. Build and maintain a pipeline of tax firms that fit our focus, from research and screening to first outreach.

- Firm analysis. Turn DATEV reports, business analyses, annual accounts and payroll data into a clear picture of revenue, clients, team capacity and profitability.

- Models and valuation. Build and maintain valuation and financing models in Excel.

- Due diligence. Prepare and run due diligence workstreams, from data room to question lists.

- Financing. Prepare materials for banks and financing partners and keep the process on track.

- Decision papers. Write investment memos and presentations for founders and investors.

- Post-merger integration. Support the onboarding of acquired firms, from process documentation to cross-firm coordination.

Requirements

- Strong academic background. You have a very good Bachelor’s degree or are enrolled in a Master’s in business, economics, finance or a related field.

- First deal experience. You’ve interned in M&A, transaction services, private equity, investment banking, corporate finance or consulting.

- Financial fluency. You understand P&Ls, balance sheets and cash flows and quickly spot what doesn’t add up.

- Analytical mindset. You turn incomplete information into a clear recommendation.

- AI-native. You use AI tools to build analyses and models faster.

- German language skills. Sellers and banks speak German, so we require fluent German (C2) and English.

Benefits

- Work directly with experienced founders. Learn first-hand from a team with backgrounds at Goldman Sachs, Harvard Business School, Bain & Company and Klarna, and from a former Y Combinator founder.

- Buy-and-build from the inside. See how a group of tax firms is built at an early stage.

- At the table. Meet sellers, banks and investors and present your own analysis.

- Ownership from day one. Take on real responsibility early, on live clients, deals and projects.

- Front-row seat to AI in the real world. See how AI transforms a traditional industry and help build it.

- Steep learning curve. Work on real problems, ship quickly and build skills that prepare you to start your own company.

- A path to stay. Strong interns get an offer to continue as working student or full-time.

The details

Full-time internship for 3 to 6 months, start any time of the year, on-site in our Berlin office five days a week.

title: Sales Operations Manager
description:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction . Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people , making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people , around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking , tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

About the Role 

Relay sells through two core motions. The first is our new-business engine: a B2B enterprise sales motion winning large retailers and brands with significant parcel volumes — and, in time, extending down-market into Small medium enterprises (SME) as that segment opens up. The second is our field engine, which grows Relay's network of "Pitstops" — local shops and businesses that act as pick-up and drop-off points where consumers can collect parcels and return items.

Both motions depend on the systems and processes this role will build and own: the account universe and TAM, lead scoring and prioritisation, outreach, CRM architecture, governance, and sales tooling.

You'll be both architect and operator, and AI-native in how you work. You'll define what great looks like across the systems and processes underpinning both sales motions, then take ownership of making it happen. You’ll also be highly fluent in metrics — using dashboards and funnel data to identify where performance is breaking down, where opportunities are being lost, and where we can drive greater efficiency.

What You'll Do 

- Build the new-business engine: own TAM, account scoring and weekly prioritisation, plus a top-of-funnel (enrichment, multi-threaded contacts, sequencing, signal-based triggers) that lets sales spend their time pitching, not hunting.

- Own the CRM and deal desk: architect Pipedrive around the selling rhythm, govern deal terms, stages and approval gates from pitch to activation, and raise the quality and speed of pitches and proposals.

- Scale the Pitstop engine: run the field team's scoring, territories, targets and dashboards, manage pricing levers and CPA, and keep lead-to-live data clean, pushing toward a self-running engine with algorithmic assignment, referrals and AI-handled inbound.

- Automate relentlessly: own the tooling stack and build-vs-buy calls (defaulting to building), strip manual work out of the sales day, and design systems that extend to SME and self-serve through configuration, not a rebuild.

- Diagnose and fix the funnel: use funnel data to find where deals stall and pipeline leaks, then ship the fixes.

Who Will Thrive in This Role 

- Systems thinker. You build systems rather than one-off fixes, and you take ideas all the way to a shipped, working solution yourself.

- Proven RevOps experience. You've run sales or revenue operations in a fast-moving environment and know what best-in-class looks like across top-of-funnel, CRM, deal desk and process.

- CRM owner, not just admin. You've implemented and evolved Pipedrive (or similar) so it fits the selling motion, rather than bending the motion to fit the tool.

- Native AI builder. You're fluent with Claude and have shipped real tooling and automations in a live business.

- Fast, practical delivery. You implement quickly and are comfortable scoping work for engineering when you need their help.

- High bar for quality. You insist on clean data and tight processes

- Equally strong in detail and with people. You're comfortable refining a workflow in depth and equally at ease talking pipeline quality with sales.

Compensation, Benefits & Workplace 

- Generous equity, richer than 99% of European startups, with annual top-ups to share Relay's success

- Private health & dental coverage, so comprehensive you'd need to be a partner at a Magic Circle law firm to match it

- 25 days of holidays

- Enhanced parental leave

- Hardware of your choice

- Extensive perks (gym subsidies, cycle-to-work, Friday office lunch, covered Uber home and dinner for late nights, and more)

- Located in Shoreditch, our office set-up enables the kind of in-person interactions that drive impact. We work 4 days on-site, with 1 day remote.

Who Thrives at Relay? 

- Aim with Precision: You define problems clearly and measure your impact meticulously.

- Play to Win: You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction.

- 1% Better Every Day : You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience.

- All In, All the Time : You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts.

- People-Powered Greatness : You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success.

- Grow the Whole Pie : You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we.

If these resonate, and you combine strong technical fundamentals with entrepreneurial drive, let’s connect.
