title: Senior Backend Engineer (Data serving)
description:
About Pleo 

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

Please note: applications will be open until Tuesday 13th October 2026 at 08.00 CEST.
We will not review any application before the closing date so please use this time to submit a high quality application. 

About the role 

We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join the Data Serving team that owns the production-grade boundary between Pleo's raw product data and everyone who consumes it, including internal product teams, AI agents, and customers directly accessing their own data. This Senior Backend Engineer role builds and owns that boundary: APIs and the low-latency serving layer underneath it. You will build customer-facing infrastructure where contract stability and latency are non-negotiable, and where the clean abstraction you maintain is what lets every downstream consumer trust the data without ever touching a raw source.

Who you’ll be working with and reporting to 

You will report to our VP of Data, and work closely with our Staff Data Platform Engineer, Data Engineers, Product Managers and others Engineers across the business. You'll also coordinate closely with the GenAI Platform and Data Infrastructure teams.

What you’ll be doing 

As a Senior Backend Engineer, you will:

- Build and own the Data API boundary: delivering clean, versioned, and performant endpoints for internal dashboards, customer-facing features, and third-party tools (e.g., Fivetran connectors via incremental syncs and cursor pagination).

- Design and optimise the read models, indexes, and caching strategies in Postgres (and future OLAP stores) to guarantee low-latency query performance.

- Build reliable integrations with Pleo’s Kotlin-based product backend services to ensure the serving layer surfaces the correct data required for a customer facing feature.

- Own the reliability and performance of the services you build: monitoring, incident response, and SLOs appropriate to customer-facing infrastructure.

- Partner with Data Engineers to define clean contracts between the ingestion/aggregation layer and the serving DB, ensuring read patterns match storage schemas.

- Partner with the Authorization team to secure APIs using industry-standard authentication and authorization protocols.

- Build a near-real-time data aggregation service to collect and unify data across Pleo services.

- Design metadata, lineage, and governance capabilities that make the serving layer explainable, auditable, and trustworthy.

- Own access control and permission management services, including row and column-level data access with full audit trails.

To put things into context, you can expect to work with the following tech stack: AWS (product side), GCP (data side), Docker, Kubernetes, BigQuery, PostgreSQL dbt, Kafka, Airflow, Python, Kotlin and more!

What you bring 

You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

- Strong backend engineering experience building and owning reporting and analytics API services and serving-layer infrastructure.

- A mindset focusing on reliability, latency, and SLOs.

- Experience owning API boundary layers including clean endpoint design, versioning, contract stability, and ensuring downstream consumers are never exposed to raw data sources.

- Strong expertise designing performant read-heavy systems, including relational database optimisation, indexing strategies, materialised views, caching, and API performance tuning.

- Solid database fundamentals (SQL and non-SQL) and strong SQL querying skills, as well as deep expertise in Kafka.

- Deep experience with a JVM-based language (Pleo's product backend is Kotlin-based).

- AWS or GCP with Kubernetes experience. You must be familiar with configuring, deploying and operating containerised applications in a k8s environment.

- Experience working at the boundary between data systems and product backend services, with a real understanding of the operational differences between the two.

- The ability to move quickly and independently. This is a hands-on delivery role with clear scope, not an architecture or advisory engagement.

- Experience in fintech, payments, or other regulated product environments.

Why is this role a good fit for you 

This role is a good fit for you if:

- You are passionate about building systems that serve other engineers.

- You understand what it means to design, build and maintain services with high performance, availability and reliability requirements.

- You have a very deep understanding of the data world and know how to bridge the gap between data and engineering.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

- You need to operate within very large and structured teams with clear hierarchy. This role sits within a small and specialist team with a lot of autonomy.

- You do not wish to be responsible for services with high availability requirements. You will be held accountable for the quality and availability of those services alongside your team.

- You prefer to be handed over clearly defined scope of work. You will be expected to define and design the solutions as much as building them.

How you’ll develop in this role 

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you will:

- Get deep into the current state: the upstream Kotlin services the serving layer will pull from, the internal consumers already waiting on the API (Data & AI Products, GenAI Platform), and any prototype serving logic that needs to be replaced or formalised.

- Ship the first production version of the Reporting API (a defined set of endpoints with agreed contracts, versioning, and SLOs) with at least one internal consumer live against it.

- Establish the access control, tenant isolation, and row/column-level security model for the API. You will have proven out low-latency query performance on Postgres, with clear metrics around reliability and SLOs, and established a clear architectural benchmark to understand when (or if) an OLAP layer would ever be necessary.

Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work . We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.

Show me the benefits 

- Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

- Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

- Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis.

- 25 days of annual leave + public holidays (additional days may apply in select countries based on local standards).

- For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options.

- We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

- Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

The interview process 

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

- Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

- Core skills test: An async AI-assisted programming test to assess your coding fundamentals.

- Hiring Manager interview: A 60-minute chat deep diving into your experience.

- Pleo Challenge: A 75-minute system design interview focusing on your architecture, infrastructure and problem-solving skills.

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

With this in mind, we want to help you understand what we really care about when reviewing your application:

- We receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI - it’s a big focus for us internally too- but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you - not AI - know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. - You will work closely with the Complaints Team, to resolve complaints about our loans, cards and auto-finance products, as well as be responsible for feeding back to both frontline and product teams on product and process improvements across the Operations Team and wider Lendable business.

We’re entering a once-in-a-company moment: a major step-change in our D2C marketing investment, a full rebrand of the company and product under the Zable brand, and a marketing function being built out at pace. This is one of the most exciting marketing builds in UK fintech right now, with the financial strength, customer base, and product depth to back it up.

Direct Mail is one of our highest-potential channels and we’re hiring a leader to turn it into a scaled, precise, and defensible growth engine. We’re looking for a Head of Direct Mail to own the channel end-to-end: creative, sends, logistics, offers, and reporting, sourcing the data pipeline and user-data enrichment that let us target the right customer, with the right offer, at the right moment.

You'll lead the channel's dedicated analysts and work with our creative team. Your job is to set the direction: decide who we mail, with what offer and when, commission and challenge the selection and response models, and hold every campaign to CAC and LTV targets.

Standalone direct mail roles with this kind of budget and autonomy are rare. If you've got significant experience in acquisition mail and want to build a channel your own way, at a profitable business with the product range and analytical capabilities to make it work, this is the role.

What we’re looking for: 

Essential: 

- 5+ years in direct mail, including at least 2–3 years owning an acquisition DM programme end to end: strategy, budget, data, production and results.

- A track record of mailing cold prospects at meaningful scale. You'll be able to talk through the volumes, budgets, response rates and CPAs you've been accountable for.

- Experience procuring data: working with data suppliers on list selection, screening, enrichment and cost.

- Deep knowledge of the DM supply chain: print, lettershop, Royal Mail products (Advertising Mail, Mailmark, partially addressed, door drops) and suppression (MPS, goneaways, deceased).

- A strongly commercial approach. You build the business case, forecast volumes and returns, own the channel P&L, and measure spend on CAC, ROI and payback rather than pieces mailed.

- Strong analytical judgement. You design test cells and holdouts, read results critically, and understand response and propensity modelling well enough to brief analysts, challenge their work and turn it into mailing decisions.

- Experience managing suppliers: tendering, negotiating, setting SLAs and keeping several partners to schedule.

- The ability to run a multi-drop campaign calendar across products, segments, creative, compliance sign-off, production and mail dates.

- Experience leading analysts and working closely with creative teams.

- A clear communicator who earns the trust of finance, risk, compliance and data teams.

- Demonstrable use of AI in your workflow.

Desirable: 

- Experience in acquisition mail in financial services, especially credit cards or loans, including prescreened or pre-approved offers and risk-based targeting.

- Experience standing up a data pipeline or enrichment stack (first-party + third-party / bureau data)

- Experience building a channel or function from scratch

- Background hiring and developing an analytics or design team

You’re a good fit if you’re: 

- Acquisition-minded: you're energised by finding new customers, not re-contacting existing ones.

- Commercially driven: you measure success in incremental LTV and payback, not response rate alone.

- A first-principles thinker: you argue from data and clean experiments, not received wisdom

- Organised: you can run several drops across multiple suppliers and still hit mailing deadlines.

- Energised by greenfield: you’d rather build the engine than tune someone else’s

What you’ll be doing 

Strategy and commercials 

- Own the direct mail strategy and set volume, response and payback targets anchored to LTV.

- Own the channel P&L: forecasting, budget and CAC/LTV discipline.

- Decide how far and how fast to scale, based on the economics.

Data and targeting 

- Source and buy prospect data from bureaus and brokers, and combine it with our first-party data.

- Direct the analysts building the response and propensity models that decide who we mail, with what offer and when.

- Work with risk analysts to shape offers around eligibility and lifetime value.

Campaigns and supplier management 

- Plan and run the campaign calendar, from data selection to the mail landing on doormats.

- Select, negotiate with and manage print and postal suppliers on cost, quality and turnaround.

- Brief the creative team on packs, copy and offers, and take them through compliance sign-off.

- Build the reporting that ties sends to funnel, revenue and LTV and report on channel performance

- Partner with data, product, risk, finance and the creative team to unlock targeting and offers

Freetrade Engineers play a pivotal role in developing and maintaining a robust, scalable platform used by thousands daily. We tackle big technical challenges, drive innovation, and build solutions that make a real impact.

Our philosophy on hiring 

We hire for engineering excellence, not just a specific list of keywords. Our interview process is language-agnostic ; we care about your ability to solve complex problems, design scalable systems, and write clean code in whichever language you’re most comfortable with.

Our stack 

Once you join, you’ll be working primarily with TypeScript, Node.js, and PostgreSQL on GCP . We don’t expect you to be an expert in these on Day 1, but we do look for engineers who are excited to master this stack and contribute to its evolution.

What you’ll do 

- Lead features from initial design and development through to post-production and validation.

- Define and uphold company-wide standards for code reviews and engineering best practices.

- Act as a senior escalation point for high-priority issues and participate in our on-call rotation.

- Constantly evaluate the tech landscape to improve our development processes and tools.

About you 

- Involve others in design decisions and delegate responsibility to help your squad grow.

- Speak candidly when quality dips and work proactively with your team to raise the bar.

- Stay calm and effective when tackling complex, ambiguous technical challenges under pressure.

- Maintain a deep obsession with the "how" and "why" of the systems you build.

- Bring a genuine interest in the world of investments and fintech.

- Stay current with industry trends to influence better internal engineering practices.

Our interview process

- Hiring Manager interview – A deep dive into your skills and experience.

- Live Coding – Show us how you think and solve problems.

description:
About Motorway

About the team

GenAI Engineering sits within Motorway's Data and AI function, alongside Machine Learning and the Machine Learning Data Platform. We own the AI features that shape how buyers and sellers experience the marketplace, from agentic workflows in the customer journey to LLM-powered tooling for our dealer network.

What we build goes into the hands of real sellers and thousands of verified dealers, usually within weeks. When it works, someone sells their car more easily. When it doesn't, we hear about it. That feedback loop is short, and it shapes how we work. We have a track record of successful deployments and a strong reputation as a result.

About the role

We're looking for a Senior GenAI Engineer to build AI applications and agentic workflows for Motorway, taking them from rapid prototype through to production-grade systems that deliver measurable value.

You'll take a problem that isn't fully defined yet and see it through to a reliable system running in production: the prompting, the retrieval, the agent design, the evals, the guardrails, the monitoring. You own that whole stack. There's no separate team who "productionises" your work later.

Most of what makes a GenAI feature good sits around the model rather than in it. The prompting is rarely the hard part. Retrieval quality is, and so is the data feeding it, evaluation you can trust, sensible behaviour when things fail, and getting it live and keeping it there. If that's the work you want to do, we're not precious about the route you took to get here. Some of us came through data science and machine learning and deliberately built up our software engineering; others came the other way.

In this role, you will:

- Own AI features end to end, from an ambiguous problem through to a reliable, observable system that real customers depend on.

- Build the retrieval and data foundations these features stand on, and treat retrieval quality as a first-class engineering problem rather than a tuning exercise.

- Design evaluation and monitoring approaches that make quality, reliability and safety measurable rather than assumed.

- Build AI applications and agents using LLMs, orchestration, APIs and data systems, applying solid production software practices throughout.

- Make the calls on models, cost and latency that shape what a feature costs us to run, and document the reasoning so others can follow it.

- Prototype quickly, work out what is reusable, and harden the patterns that work into components the rest of the team adopts.

- Raise the quality of the work around you through code review, design feedback and the standards you set by example.

- Represent your technical decisions directly to product managers and stakeholders, translating model behaviour into business consequence.

About you

- You've shipped AI or ML systems that real users depend on, and you've stayed close enough to production to know how they behave when they break.

- Strong Python, and SQL you genuinely use. A lot of this work is data work: assembling grounding data, building golden datasets, and digging into why something failed.

- You've invested deliberately in your software engineering craft: testing, error handling, CI/CD, observability, and the MLOps practices that keep things healthy once they're live.

- You're hands-on across the GenAI stack: LLM APIs, retrieval and vector stores, agents with tool use, and structured outputs, running on cloud infrastructure (we use AWS and GCP).

- You have a real point of view on evaluation, most likely because you've been caught out by a system that looked fine and wasn't.

- You can reason about how models fail, including hallucination and prompt injection, and what that means for someone who trusts the output.

- You know when to reach for a model, when something simpler will do, and when to stop.

- You're a constructive reviewer, and colleagues are better off for having worked alongside you.

You could be a great fit if

- You're curious about how things actually work, and you follow that curiosity past the first plausible answer.

- You're drawn to problems where the right approach isn't obvious yet.

- You're honest about the limits of what you know and pull people in early rather than late.

- You take responsibility for what you ship, watch how it behaves, and fix it when it breaks.

- You get satisfaction from the unglamorous work that makes an AI feature actually good, not just the part that demos well.

- You can disagree well, and commit once a decision is made.

Benefits

We've got your back, in life's biggest moments and the everyday ones too.

title: CDI - Senior Product Engineer - Paris
description:
Mission 

Ce que vous construisez ne reste pas à l’état de démonstration : de vrais utilisateurs, au sein de grands groupes, s’en servent chaque jour. Applications et agents se conçoivent et s’exploitent en binôme avec l’AI Product Manager. Une équipe sinistres retrouve ainsi sur un seul écran les documents utiles et un brouillon de réponse ; ailleurs, un processus de commande ne demande plus aucune ressaisie manuelle.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez que de vrais utilisateurs s’appuient sur ce que vous livrez. 

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype Product Engineer.

Activités et responsabilités 

À chaque projet, l’AI Product Manager pilote le produit avec le client : ce qui se construit en premier, et la vérification que les utilisateurs s’en servent, se décident à deux.

Autour de l’application, trois métiers se croisent : les AI Engineers pour le comportement du modèle, les Platform Engineers pour le déploiement, les Context & Analytics Engineers pour les données dont l’application a besoin. Les tests se font avec les utilisateurs finaux, le code se relit entre pairs et les nouvelles recrues sont accompagnées.

Vos responsabilités : 

- 
Construire des applications métier : front end, back end et API.

- 
Intégrer des agents et des assistants dans un processus métier, avec des contrôles humains là où ils comptent.

- 
Automatiser des processus de bout en bout.

- 
Intégrer un modèle dans un outil que les équipes utilisent déjà.

- 
Construire les connecteurs dont le cas d’usage a besoin, par exemple un serveur MCP pour un outil métier.

- 
Concevoir l’expérience utilisateur de l’IA : quand une personne valide, comment afficher les sources et l’incertitude.

- 
Définir avec l’AI Product Manager les évaluations propres au cas d’usage et les suivre en production.

- 
Assumer ce que vous livrez après la mise en production : monitoring, incidents, adoption.

Profil recherché 

Les indispensables : 

- 
Vous avez construit des applications avec un front end, un back end et des API, même si votre expertise est plus marquée d’un côté.

- 
Du code testé, relu et documenté, en Python, TypeScript ou dans un langage similaire.

- 
Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

- 
Des besoins d’utilisateurs transformés en une première version, puis améliorée à partir de leurs retours.

- 
Le monitoring, les incidents et l’adoption font, pour vous, partie du métier.

- 
Une aisance à expliquer vos choix techniques à des personnes non techniques.

Un plus, pas un prérequis : 

- 
Une expérience de construction d’agents ou d’assistants au-dessus d’un LLM : appel d’outils, orchestration.

- 
Une expérience de conception de parcours avec validation humaine (human-in-the-loop) ou d’interfaces d’IA.

- 
Une expérience d’intégration à des logiciels métier, comme un ERP ou un CRM.

- 
Une expérience au contact des clients.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? 

Entre le produit, l’interface et le modèle, le Product Engineer occupe le point où l’IA rencontre ses utilisateurs. Leurs réactions s’observent directement, et chaque version livrée tient compte de ce que les usages ont révélé.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’apprend sur les projets : conception d’agents, évaluation par cas d’usage, expérience utilisateur de l’IA, avec l’appui des AI Engineers et de la communauté Product Engineer. À partir de 2027, l’archétype Product Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (évaluation de l’IA, responsabilité en production).

Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme le chapter AI Product Manager.

Processus de recrutement 

Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.

- 
Entretien RH (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.

- 
Appel avec le CTO (15 à 30 min, à distance).

- 
Screening technique (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.

- 
Code review et live coding (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.

- 
Cas technique (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.

- 
Entretien final (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.

Selon les étapes, tous les outils d’IA sont autorisés, ou aucun. Lors du live coding, c’est la manière de travailler avec l’assistance de l’IA qui est observée.

Rémunération : 60 000€ à 70 000€ brut annuel (fixe) + jusqu’à 6 000€ de variable selon expérience et séniorité

Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l’adéquation avec le rôle.

If you thrive in fast-paced environments and you want to help shape how the next generation of fans experience sports, you’re in the right place. We’re on track to become the global leader in sports media, and this is definitely the best time to join our adventure. 

💡 Overview

title: Product Marketing Manager
description:
About Nabla 

Nabla delivers a unified clinical AI platform used by healthcare organizations across specialties and care settings. The platform includes:

Ambient AI documentation that captures clinical conversations and generates structured notes.

AI-powered dictation and clinical workflow tools embedded directly within EHR systems.

Agentic AI capabilities that support multi-step clinical and administrative tasks.

Enterprise-grade infrastructure built for secure deployment across health systems.

About the Role

The Product Marketing Manager will own how Nabla positions, launches, and drives adoption of the product with clinicians across their entire journey — from onboarding and activation through engagement and retention.

This is product marketing where the message ships directly to the user. You own the narrative for every new feature launch, then own the in-app and email programs that turn that narrative into activation.

You'll define the segmentation, write the positioning, ship the campaigns, and measure whether they actually moved adoption.

Userpilot is in place, but everything around it still needs to be built: the activation and adoption strategy, in-app and email templates, segmentation, cohort analysis, the process with Product Marketing peers, CSM, PM, and Design, and the campaign calendar.

This is a hands-on, highly operational PMM role. We need someone who lives in the tools, is data-driven, can test fast, structure the process, and turn usage insights into concrete positioning and messaging decisions.

Userpilot is the first step. Over time, this person will take ownership of the full communication stack across email, in-app, and other channels. The role works extremely closely with Product Marketing peers, Design, PM, Data, and Product Ops.

Nabla serves two distinct audiences, and lifecycle programs must work for both:

- Self-serve clinicians , who discover, activate, and adopt the product largely on their own. Here, automated email and in-app communication carries most of the relationship — your messaging is the go-to-market motion.

- Mid-market and enterprise health systems , managed by CSMs. Here the human relationship leads, and your programs must arm and reinforce the CSM — giving them timing, context, and content, never working around them.

You'll design each lifecycle so the right channel leads for each segment. On top of this, healthtech is a highly regulated industry with demanding clients: every communication must meet a high bar for accuracy, security, and professionalism, while still feeling personal and useful to busy clinicians.

Responsibilities

Feature Launch Positioning & Activation 

- Own weekly in-app launch communication for new features, end to end and at a fast cadence

- Define the positioning and messaging for each release — what it is, why a clinician should care, what changes in their day

- Design the in-app experience (placement, format, flow) for each launch

- Validate messaging with Product Marketing peers, PM, and Design before shipping

- Launch on time and coordinate across the relevant teams

- Track performance (reach, engagement, adoption) for every launch and iterate quickly on results

- Stay highly reactive to the product roadmap, turning new releases into clear, well-timed clinician communication

Lifecycle Strategy and Execution 

- Own the full lifecycle strategy across onboarding, activation, engagement, and retention, ensuring each stage of the practitioner journey is intentional, personalized, and measurable

- Tailor segmentation, messaging, and cadence to the distinct needs of each segment:

- For self-serve, build automated email and in-app programs that drive activation, adoption, and retention with minimal human touch

- For mid-market and enterprise, build programs that complement and support CSMs

- Direct and execute creative strategy for lifecycle channels — briefing, reviewing, and optimizing copy and design for brand consistency and message effectiveness

- Build and maintain a clear campaign calendar across functions

Experimentation and Analytics 

- Lead a rigorous experimentation roadmap: A/B and multivariate testing of messaging, creative, cadence, segmentation, and value propositions

- Define and own lifecycle KPIs, building reporting frameworks and sharing regular performance insights with marketing and cross-functional leadership

- Partner with Data and Analytics on audience segmentation, behavioral signals, and AI-driven insights to enhance personalization at scale

- Turn cohort and usage insights into concrete messaging and product-marketing actions

Cross-functional Collaboration 

- Collaborate with Product Marketing peers, Design, PM, Data, Product Ops, Clinical, and Brand to align lifecycle programs with broader business goals and the practitioner experience

- Establish a clear, repeatable process across Product Marketing, CSM, PM, and Design for planning and shipping campaigns

- Ensure all programs are developed and executed in compliance with HIPAA and applicable federal and state laws, partnering with Legal and Compliance as needed

Operations and Tooling 

- Take ownership of the full communication stack, starting with Userpilot

- Evaluate and manage lifecycle marketing technology partnerships, recommending optimizations as we scale

- Build and maintain process documentation, campaign playbooks, and training materials on internal platforms

- Leverage AI tools as a core part of daily work (drafting, research, iteration) to improve efficiency, quality, and decision-making

What We Are Looking For 

- 3-5 years in B2B product marketing, lifecycle marketing, or product-led growth marketing, including hands-on ownership of in-app channels

- Proven ability to craft positioning and messaging for product launches and to ship it yourself, not hand it off

- Deep expertise across the full post-signup funnel (onboarding, activation, engagement, retention)

- Strong Product DNA, with sharp attention to user workflows and the details that shape the product experience

- Strong strategic and analytical thinking, with the ability to translate complex data into clear hypotheses, actionable insights, and business recommendations

- Strong cross-functional collaboration skills; ability to manage stakeholder expectations, influence without authority, and build alignment across diverse teams

- Track record of building and scaling programs that drove measurable growth in adoption, engagement, and retention

- Comfortable in a highly regulated, high-stakes industry (healthtech) with demanding clients, where accuracy, security, and compliance are non-negotiable

Nice to have: 

- Hands-on experience with Userpilot and HubSpot

- Familiarity with Looker, Tableau, Mixpanel, Amplitude, or similar

- Experience in a regulated industry: healthcare, behavioral health, or health-adjacent

- Experience with AI-powered personalization, segmentation tools, or ML-informed campaign optimization

- Experience marketing to a professional or clinical end user

Life at Nabla 

When you join Nabla, you join a team that is driven by excellence, curiousity, and kindness. Together, we’re committed to making clinicians’ lives easier and improving healthcare experiences for everyone. We believe clinicians should be able to focus on what they were trained to do, caring for their patients, and that no patient should feel their visit was rushed. 

We work hard and make time to have fun, too. Our #nablabla channel is just as active as #feature-show-off . We support well-being with workday activities at least three times a week; choose from yoga, running, Pilates, or HIIT. We also host regular off-sites, meet up across New York, Paris, San Francisco, and other cities, and keep the chocolate and nuts well stocked.

If this sounds like an environment where you’ll thrive, we look forward to reading your application.

Our Values at Nabla 

Joining Nabla means being part of a team that shares a commitment to excellence, humility, growth, and inclusion.

Every day is a new chance to excel 

We aim for nothing less than the best and are willing to put in the effort and dedication required to exceed standards. We learn from yesterday’s failures and do better every day.

Stay humble 

There’s no place for ego in our team. Our collective success is more important than individual achievements. We see humility as wisdom — keeping focus on the bigger picture.

Feedback is a gift 

We embrace feedback and foster a culture of trust and respect that helps everyone grow. We communicate openly about both achievements and challenges, and we actively involve each other in finding solutions.

Committed to diversity 

We recognize the ongoing challenge of diversity in tech. Our responsibility starts with fostering an inclusive environment where everyone feels empowered to be their authentic selves and do their best work.

Diversity & Inclusion 

Diversity and inclusivity are fundamental values at Nabla. We embrace individuals from various backgrounds, including race, gender, educational history, sexual orientation, and beyond.

As an equal opportunity employer, we actively seek out and welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds, believing that a wide range of perspectives enriches our team and enhances our ability to innovate and thrive.

Avoid recruitment scams: Stay safe and informed

There is an active employment and financial scam which uses Nabla to collect personal information. If you’re contacted by a Nabla recruiter, please ensure they are utilizing a nabla.com email address. We will never ask for the exchange of any money or credit card details during the recruitment process. Nabla utilizes a hiring platform for all applications; please be aware of any suspicious email activity. You can find more information following this link .

Nabla does not accept unsolicited CVs from recruiters or employment agencies in response to the Nabla Careers page or a Nabla social media post. Any unsolicited CVs, including those submitted directly to hiring managers, are deemed to be the property of Nabla.

- Structured problem-solving: you diagnose with data, run tool selections or RFPs, and turn recommendations into changes that stick.

- A playbook to build: help create and refine our finance transformation playbook, challenge existing processes and shape how we work.

- How we work: a data-driven, hands-on culture, with high autonomy and access to senior leaders when needed.

- Tools we use: our Finance stack includes SAP ERP Cloud, Coupa, Kyriba, Amelkis, and Anaplan.

- Communication & synthesis: You communicate clearly in writing and in conversation, and can structure and present your ideas to a range of stakeholders.

- Project & stakeholder management: You can lead cross-functional projects, build alignment across teams and break down silos to move priorities forward.

- Languages: Fluency in Italian and English is required.

- Team & impact: Join the Strategy team and play a key role in shaping Qonto’s strategy and driving strategic projects in Italy.

title: AI Engineer - Full time
description:
TLDR; Davis is hiring an AI Engineer to work on the multi-agent pipeline turning raw, fragmented data into expert-grade real estate deliverables. You will make it more reliable, fast, and indistinguishable from the best human teams, then push it past what any human team could do, owning the stack end to end, from context engineering and orchestration to verification, storage and evaluation.

About Davis 

Davis is an AI-native real estate company accelerating early-stage development and architectural design. Today developers coordinate 4-5 fragmented stakeholders over weeks or months. Soon they'll need only one: Davis.

We turn every input that shapes a development decision into decision-ready outputs: investor-grade feasibility studies, investment analysis, and architect-certified designs, delivered in days. Every stage pairs our proprietary AI systems with expert review, so velocity never comes at the cost of reliability.

We closed a $5.5M pre-seed co-led by Heartcore Capital and Balderton Capital , with Yellow, Evantic and Entrepreneur First, alongside angels from the founding teams of Spacemaker, Black Forest Labs, Hugging Face, Supabase, Cleo and Spore Bio. We already work with leading developers and expect to support hundreds of projects over the coming year, deepening our research, our hiring, and our coverage of the development process end to end.

Where We Operate 

Early-stage development starts with a chain of high-stakes decisions , each requiring different data, different expertise, and different deliverables. Today, we deliver AI-powered outputs across the full spectrum - site sourcing, feasibility studies, architectural design, investment analysis, financial modeling, dataroom analysis, and more.

The Role 

You will work on one of the core systems behind what Davis delivers. Our agents take raw, fragmented data and turn it into deliverables that real estate professionals use to make high-stakes decisions. Your job is to make that pipeline reliable, fast, and indistinguishable from work done by the best human teams - then push it beyond what any human team could do.

You can expect to:

- Build and operate multi-agent systems that turn heterogeneous data into expert-grade deliverables across real estate development workflows.

- Own the system end to end : infra, orchestration, context engineering, how the system selects, structures, and injects the right information so agents behave reliably at scale.

- Ensure production-grade quality , performance, and reliability across every output we deliver to clients.

- Sit with clients and domain experts regularly to understand their constraints, challenge your own assumptions, and make sure every output meets and even exceeds clients' expectations.

Beyond the technical depth, this role will expose you to how real estate decisions are made, how clients think, and what it takes to deliver outputs they trust. You'll develop a sharp business intuition alongside your engineering skills.

Key Responsibilities 

- Harness engineering: design and build the system layer around the model - context assembly, tool orchestration, verification, and report generation - to deliver consistent, high-quality outputs at scale.

- Data ingestion & context assembly: handle messy, unstructured project data from heterogeneous sources and ensure agents have the right context at all times.

- Storage & traceability: persist sources, extracted facts, intermediate results, report versions, and expert edits.

- Expert-in-the-loop UX: design and build the review experience (annotations, edits, approvals, diffs/version history, provenance display).

- Evaluation & benchmarking: build an internal eval harness (datasets, rubrics, regression tests, monitoring) to track agents performance over time.

What We're Looking For 

- 1.5+ years building and deploying production software at scale (APIs, reliability, testing, performance).

- Experience building and evaluating LLM agents / multi-step workflows in real systems.

- Proven context engineering experience: you've built systems where reliability depends on assembling the right context (RAG over heterogeneous sources, summarization, conversation state, tool outputs).

- Deep Python expertise (clean architecture, typing, async/concurrency, strong testing culture).

- Strong experience with databases + data modeling (structured storage, document storage, versioning).

- Full-stack experience (you can ship a real UI), with a clear backend emphasis .

- Comfortable building from first principles: we don't want heavy agent frameworks — we prefer a lightweight, well-engineered codebase.

Nice to Have 

- Experience operating LLM systems with observability and quality monitoring in production.

- GIS familiarity (parcels, zoning layers, geocoding).

- Multi-country product experience (heterogeneous sources, localization, varying rules).

- NLP background

Why Join Us 

You're joining a team of 9 at the very beginning - where every decision you make shapes the product, the culture, and the trajectory of the company. What you build here will be yours.

- Direct impact on growth: your work doesn't sit behind three layers of review. You ship, clients use it, and you see the results. Every output you improve translates directly into revenue and reputation.

- Real-world impact : your work supports investment decisions, accelerates development timelines, and helps redefine how cities are imagined, designed, and built.

- High ownership : own the full feasibility stack end to end, as the CEO of that part.

- Competitive salary and meaningful equity in an early-stage company.

- A small team with high standards - we ship fast and love working together.

More information about Davis, the team and the market we’re going after: 

Team 

Mehdi (Co-founder & CEO) grew up in a family of architects and has lived this problem firsthand. He's a repeat founder who bootstrapped his first startup at 20 , and graduated from Sciences Po and HEC Paris. Amine (Co-founder & CTO) is an AI researcher from École Polytechnique who worked extensively on discrete diffusion and turned down a PhD with Google DeepMind to build Davis . They started working together in July 2025 at Entrepreneur First's first European residency, a two-month lock-in in a German castle.

Today we're a team of 12 : technical profiles from Polytechnique, ENS and INRIA alongside architects and deep real estate expertise.

We're small with an extremely high bar . If you want to work deeply on hard problems and see your work reach clients within days, you're the one we need.

Why We'll Win 

Real estate is a $13 trillion industry that technology has largely bypassed. The professional services that feed it (design, engineering, feasibility, permitting) represent hundreds of billions in spend that no one has seriously automated.

Proptech spent the last decade selling SaaS on the edges of these workflows. It didn't work, for two reasons: no professional wants another tool to learn, and no tool can automate work that runs on expert judgment. Davis makes a different bet. We don't sell tools, we sell the work: AI-generated, expert-validated, delivered in days instead of weeks. Every project compounds our data advantage across typologies, geographies and regulatory contexts.

Why No One Has Solved Architectural Design Yet 

Real estate development bleeds time and money in architectural design loops. Architects cycle through dozens of floorplan revisions to meet regulatory and client constraints, each round taking days, each missed constraint restarting the loop. Traditional CAD and BIM tools offer zero generative capability ; parametric tools only check constraints after generation , leading to designs that frequently break under new zoning rules or irregular sites.

Generative AI has the potential to solve this , but doesn't yet. Fine-tuning image diffusion models on floorplans produces layouts that look plausible but fall apart under scrutiny: hallucinated rooms, mislabeled spaces, code violations no architect would accept. Pixel-space models have no concept of what a wall is or why a corridor needs to connect two things. Compliance-guidance techniques typically require segmentation at each noisy timestep, compounding errors and making major edits impractical. As a result, floorplans may “look” plausible but break building codes, or need heavy post-processing before they're usable.

We care about who you are, not just what's on your CV. 

If you're drawn to what we're building but don't meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. Studies show that women in particular tend to apply only when they meet 100% of the criteria. If that's you, please don't let that hold you back. We'd love to receive your application.

title: Change and Transformation Manager - Client Delivery (Fluency in French & English required)
description:
Change and Transformation Manager – Client Delivery (French/english) 

Location: Paris, France (hybrid, three days a week in the office; occasional travel to Brussels and London)
Level: Programme Manager senior 
Team: Client Delivery
Contract: Permanent
Reporting To: Operating Model Design Lead

Please note: This role is based in France, so you need to live here or be open to relocating, and it requires an existing right to work in the EU. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities. 

Fluent French and English (spoken and written) are essential, and we kindly ask you to submit your CV in English. 

About Kaluza 

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.

What you’ll do 

- Own change and transformation support for go-live readiness for ENGIE France’s migration onto Kaluza as the hands-on lead, from planning through cutover, hypercare and transition towards scaling, so ENGIE’s teams are ready and confident to adopt the platform from day one.

- Decide the change approach for the programme: stakeholder analysis, change impact assessment, training design and business readiness engagement, shaped to ENGIE France’s operating context and owned by their teams.

- Operate Kaluza’s business readiness governance: stage gates, readiness evidence, risk and dependency tracking and weekly reporting.

- Partner with the Learning and Adoption Specialist in France to coordinate training, Train the Trainer and knowledge content, so enablement lands throughout each programme increment as we build out and release features via Agile delivery.

- Be the day-to-day point of contact for ENGIE France on business readiness, change and adoption, giving practical change advice to their transformation leads.

- Track adoption and operational stability through hypercare, root-cause any shortfall against acceptance criteria, and agree interventions with ENGIE.

- Improve Kaluza’s readiness playbook: evolve what worked on ENGIE Belgium, test fixes where it falls short in France, and share what you learn with colleagues across Client Delivery to shape the platform’s operational foundations and improvements and to set our global standards.

Day to day, the activities you’ll lead or support include:

- Change impact and readiness planning: diagnosing the full scope of impacts across roles, workflows, systems and customer experience, then turning them into a prioritised readiness plan sequenced against delivery, migration and release cadence.

- Stakeholders, sponsors and change networks: mapping stakeholders and influence at workstream level, helping sponsors stay visible and engaged, and shaping the champion, superuser and people-manager networks that carry change into ENGIE’s business.

- Communications and resistance: supporting ENGIE France’s own communications and engagement strategy, so their teams and customers hear a consistent, positive story about the programme. You’ll help leaders and champions advocate for the change, internally and with customers, and anticipate where resistance may form so you can intervene before it becomes entrenched.

- Migration and go-live readiness: building the business and operational readiness evidence that enables a smooth transfer to service, measured against the agreed acceptance criteria, and supporting the go-live command centre.

- Hypercare and stabilisation: agreeing hypercare entry and exit criteria, monitoring stability and adoption signals, and handing over cleanly to ENGIE’s business-as-usual teams.

- Early releases and workarounds: planning for known limitations in early releases, and reflecting them in training, knowledge and communications so users are never caught by surprise. You’ll work with Release Management so each platform release arrives with the enablement it needs.

What you’ll bring 

Ideally, you’ll have:

- Several years of hands-on change delivery on large platform or systems transformations, with a recognised change management discipline. You solve a wide range of problems creatively and work with little supervision.

- Experience in regulated, customer-facing operational environments, including live customer account migration, cutover and go-live, where you have shaped the approach rather than only followed one.

- Strong communication and stakeholder management, credible with client programme leads and transformation sponsors.

- Fluency in French and English, written and spoken.

- Comfort working with data: you explore adoption and programme data yourself, report on it clearly and challenge decisions when evidence is weak.

- Commercial awareness: you understand how Kaluza makes money and balance what the client needs against cost, working alongside SI partners and the client’s own change resources without duplicating effort.

What will set you apart: a background in energy retail or utilities, vendor-side experience on a SaaS implementation, and/or knowledge of contact centre operations and technology.

Our Values 

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

- Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

- Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

- Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

- Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

- Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.

Our Perks 

- Financial & Insurance: Discretionary bonus, Alan Mutuelle Health Insurance, x3 Life & Death insurance (Prévoyance) via Alan, and standard Sécurité Sociale contributions (pension, family allowance, unemployment insurance)

- Allowances: 50% commuting expense reimbursement, €200 Home Working Allowance, and €150 Learning Fund

- Time Off & Flexibility: 25 days holiday + bank holidays + RTT days, Moments That Matter Leave, Compassionate Leave, two paid Volunteering Days, Flexible Working, and Career Break eligibility

Come as you are 

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

title: ML Hydrologist, Flood Forecasting
description:
About the Role
Global ML flood models now outperform traditional approaches on large rivers, but they still break down in the small, fast catchments where flash floods happen. Riverkin, a VC-backed ETH Zürich Spin-off, is closing that gap. We start from hydrological models trained across thousands of catchments worldwide and make them accurate locally, using a sensor network we deploy ourselves in exactly the places public datasets don't reach.

We are looking for an ML hydrologist to own that work. You will report to the CTO and work directly with our other hydrologist, who covers rainfall radar and short-term nowcasting.

Why this is interesting 

- Data nobody else has: Our own field-deployed sensors give you live streamflow observations in small, previously ungauged catchments.

- An open problem: Whether large-sample models can be made reliable at flash-flood scale is unsolved, and you would be working on it with real data and real users.

- Built to protect lives and critical infrastructure: Your models will power early flood warning systems safeguarding hydropower plants and giving first responders more time to protect communities

- Publishing and open source: We encourage publishing results and contributing to open tools such as NeuralHydrology and Caravan.

- Compute: GPU resources are available for training and experimentation.

What You'll Do 

- Bring global flood models to the local scale

- Take state-of-the-art hydrological ML models (LSTMs, Transformers) trained on large-sample datasets and adapt them to the catchments our customers care about.

- Use our own sensor data alongside public gauge, reanalysis and radar data to fine-tune and validate those models locally.

- Tackle prediction in ungauged and data-scarce basins through transfer learning and regionalisation.

- Own hydrological modelling end to end: set the technical direction, decide when to adapt pre-trained models or train our own, and lead the work from experimentation through validation to production.

- Work as one modelling team

- Make practical trade-offs between forecast accuracy, model complexity and development effort to build a reliable product that meets customer needs.

- Work side by side with our hydrologist specialising in rainfall radar and nowcasting to directly integrate rainfall nowcasts into your flood models.

- Work with software engineers to put models into production and monitor their performance.

- Identify and test advances in ML flood forecasting, turning promising research into more accurate and reliable forecasts for our customers.

- Stay close to the real world

- We believe the best modellers understand the world behind their models. We encourage you to join field deployments and customer conversations to build that understanding firsthand.

- You are an opinionated contributor to key technical decisions.

Who You Are 

- You’ve built and validated hydrological ML models across many catchments and have experience taking modelling work into real-world use.

- You combine scientific rigour with product judgement: you test assumptions, understand uncertainty and focus on improvements that matter to customers.

- You take ownership from an open question to a working solution. You set priorities, make decisions and keep moving without waiting for perfect information.

- You care deeply about the quality of your work. You dig into why models fail, follow problems through and stay invested in how your forecasts perform after deployment.

- You communicate clearly in writing and in person, can explain your reasoning and trade-offs, and work closely with people across hydrology, software, hardware and field operations.

Technical Requirements 

- Hands-on experience training or fine-tuning ML streamflow or flood models across many catchments at once (regional, continental or global), for example on CAMELS or Caravan. Experience with single-catchment models alone is not sufficient.

- Experience transferring such models to new or data-scarce catchments through fine-tuning, regionalisation, or prediction in ungauged basins.

- Strong understanding of rainfall-runoff processes and the limitations of hydrological observations and input data.

- Experience validating models across unseen catchments and time periods, including assessing flood-peak magnitude, timing and predictive uncertainty.

- Strong Python skills, with experience writing maintainable code for data processing, modelling and reproducible experiments.

- Practical depth in deep learning for time series, including developing, training and debugging models in PyTorch or a comparable framework.

- MSc or PhD in hydrology, water resources, atmospheric sciences, machine learning, or equivalent.

Nice to Have 

- Publications or open-source work on large-sample hydrology, transfer learning, or ungauged-basin prediction.

- Experience with NeuralHydrology, ERA5 or similar global forcing datasets.

- Experience with sub-daily or event-based flood modelling.

- Experience processing large hydrometeorological datasets with tools such as xarray and Dask, and formats such as Zarr.

- Previous early startup experience.

Role Details 

- Contract: Permanent, full-time (100% FTE).

- Start date: immediately

- Reports to : CTO.

- Compensation : Commensurate with experience + equity

- Growth : a key early hire with the opportunity to shape Riverkin's flood modelling as the team grows.

- Location: Four days per week in our Zurich office and one day working from home.

- Work authorisation : Swiss or EU/EFTA citizenship, or a valid Swiss work permit, is required.

- Working language: English. German is not required.

About Riverkin
We are a well-capitalized Swiss startup building real-time sensing and data infrastructure for rivers. Our own field-deployed sensors collect live water-level and sediment data, while our platform turns that data into decision-ready insights for customers. We work directly with the hydropower sector, where predicting flash floods is needed for daily operations. As we prove ourselves in this field, we will move towards the first responders market. We are a small, hands-on team working across hydrology, hardware, field engineering, software and market development.

title: IT Reliability Engineer

Du sorgst dafür, dass Systeme zuverlässig betrieben werden, technische Risiken frühzeitig erkannt werden und Monitoring-, Backup-, Update- sowie Lifecycle-Prozesse nachhaltig funktionieren. Die Themen Monitoring, Betriebsstabilität, Lifecycle-Management und technische Qualitätsstandards haben bei MDigital bereits heute einen hohen Stellenwert und werden aktiv durch unser Engineering-Team gelebt. Aufgrund des Unternehmenswachstums und der zunehmenden Bedeutung dieser Aufgaben investieren wir nun gezielt in eine spezialisierte Rolle innerhalb des Engineering-Teams.

Mit dem weiteren Wachstum des Unternehmens besteht zudem die Perspektive, den Bereich IT Reliability Engineering langfristig weiter auszubauen und zusätzliche Mitarbeitende in diesem Umfeld zu etablieren.

Monitoring & Infrastruktur

- Analyse, Priorisierung und Nachverfolgung von Warnmeldungen

- Sicherstellung der vollständigen Integration produktiver Systeme ins Monitoring

- Förderung von Standardisierung und Automatisierung im täglichen Betrieb

- Analyse wiederkehrender Incidents und Erarbeitung nachhaltiger Lösungen

Backup & Recovery 

- Sicherstellung funktionierender Backup- und Recovery-Prozesse

- Nachverfolgung fehlerhafter Sicherungen

- Integration neuer Systeme in bestehende Backup-Konzepte

- Planung, Durchführung und Dokumentation regelmässiger Restore-Tests

Client-, Server- & Update-Management 

- Überwachung des Update- und Sicherheitsstatus von Clients und Servern

- Sicherstellung aktueller Sicherheits- und Systemstände

- Standardisierung und Automatisierung von Update-Prozessen

- Verwaltung von Serversystemen über Microsoft Azure Arc

- Verwaltung von Clients über Microsoft Intune und bestehende Endpoint-Management-Lösungen

- Förderung einer möglichst zentralisierten und automatisierten Systemverwaltung

Evergreen & Lifecycle Management 

- Überwachung von EOL- und EOS-Systemen

- Kontrolle von Firmware-, Software- und Security-Ständen

- Identifikation technischer und sicherheitsrelevanter Altlasten

- Erarbeitung von Handlungsempfehlungen für Engineering und Management

- Unterstützung von Standardisierungsinitiativen

Lizenz-, Zertifikats- & Vertragsüberwachung 

- Überwachung von SSL-Zertifikaten und Laufzeiten

- Kontrolle von Softwarelizenzen und Wartungsverträgen

- Frühzeitige Meldung bevorstehender Verlängerungen

- Vermeidung betrieblicher Risiken durch ablaufende Lizenzen oder Zertifikate

- Nachvollziehbare Dokumentation relevanter Informationen

Dokumentation & Betriebsqualität 

- Pflege und Weiterentwicklung technischer Kundendokumentationen

- Erstellung und Aktualisierung von Betriebsanleitungen

- Dokumentation neuer Systeme und Änderungen

- Sicherstellung eines nachvollziehbaren und professionellen Betriebsstandards

- Unterstützung bei der Kommunikation kritischer technischer Ereignisse

Pikettdienst und Team-Integration 

Als Teil unseres Engineering-Teams beteiligst du dich am rotierenden Pikettdienst und hilfst mit, den stabilen Betrieb unserer Kundenumgebungen auch ausserhalb der regulären Arbeitszeiten sicherzustellen. Die Teilnahme am Pikettdienst wird entsprechend geplant und vergütet.

Benefits

title: Senior Solutions Engineer | Switzerland | Remote
description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . 

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

We share our technical and product expertise with customers through demos, hands on enablement, presentations, technical evaluations and ongoing interaction. We partner closely with our Sales team to help qualify and close opportunities. The Solutions Engineering team is one of the primary routes of communication from our customers to the Product Management and Engineering teams. 

A Solutions Engineer is able to really listen to a prospect or customer, understand their requirements, ask the right questions to extract as much information as required and translate all that into a solution with Grafana Labs technology. They are the bridge between the highly technical engineering folks here at Grafana Labs, our customers and our Sales team.

- You love solving technical challenges and thrive on bringing creative solutions to our customers

Bonus Points For:

title: Senior AI Engineer - VLA Foundation Model
description:
RIVR, part of Amazon is a robotics company pioneering Physical AI through real-world doorstep delivery. Founded in 2024 as an ETH Zurich spin-off, RIVR developed wheeled-legged robots designed to operate in complex, unstructured environments such as stairs, gates, doors, and uneven urban terrain. We believe that achieving general physical intelligence requires solving real customer problems in the real world, where robots can learn from rich operational data at scale.

Following our acquisition by Amazon in March 2026, we are continuing this mission with greater reach and speed. By combining custom robot hardware, onboard autonomy, and cloud-based coordination, RIVR, part of Amazon is building the next generation of safe, reliable autonomous robots for last-mile delivery

Job Description 

Our fleet of delivery robots operates globally today, generating vast amounts of robotic real-world data. By utilizing state-of-the-art Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, large-scale generalist models (like Transformers), generative AI, and similar methods, we can leverage this pool of data to significantly enhance its autonomy, navigation, and manipulation skills. In this role, you will develop multi-modal models that enable robots to autonomously generate actions from demonstrations, real-time sensor data, and natural language commands. We are seeking an expert in VLA models, imitation learning, and generative AI techniques with a deep knowledge of supervised, and self-supervised learning algorithms. If you are passionate about pushing the boundaries of AI we invite you to join us in shaping the future of intelligent robotics. 

What you’ll be doing 

- Develop and implement cutting-edge Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, generalist robot transformers, and imitation learning algorithms (e.g., diffusion policies) to enable robots to autonomously execute complex tasks.

- Design, test, and refine your algorithms to meet the demands of complex real-world autonomy and navigation tasks, with a focus on spatial reasoning and generalization.

- Streamline the data collection and training workflow to efficiently expand model capabilities with new tasks and data sources.

- Collaborate with the reinforcement learning team to innovate methods that leverage both simulated and real-world data.

- Optimize and distill networks for real-time deployment on the edge (e.g. Nvidia Jetson Thor).

- Build, lead and mentor an exceptional team of software engineers.

- Provide expert guidance to product managers and executives for strategic decision-making.

- Create and maintain documentation, guidelines, and best practices to streamline knowledge sharing.

What you must have 

- Master’s degree or higher in a relevant field such as Engineering, Robotics, or Machine Learning.

- A minimum of three years of industry or research experience, with PhD experience applicable.

- Strong deep learning fundamentals including supervised learning, self-supervised learning, Transformer-based architectures, policy optimization algorithms, imitation learning, and generative AI techniques (including Diffusion Models).

- Proven experience in developing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models or large-scale generalist robot models (e.g., RT-2, Octo, etc.).

- Strong background in robotics including autonomy, navigation.

- Experience with deploying artificial neural networks on hardware platforms.

- Ability to prototype algorithms and train deep neural networks in Python (Pytorch)

Get some bonus points 

- PhD degree in Robotics, Engineering, Computer Science, Machine Learning or a similar discipline, or an equivalent amount of research experience.

- Publications at top-tier conferences.

- Experience in managing a software team.

- Ability to write production-level code in modern C++

RIVR, part of Amazon is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team that values every perspective. If you’re passionate about driving innovation in robotics and creating meaningful impact, we encourage you to apply and bring your unique self to our team.

We believe the best work is done when collaborating and therefore require in-person presence in our office locations.

title: Senior Airspace Engineer
description:
About Electra 

Air travel is about to become something more: more direct, more accessible, and more connected to the places where people live, work and want to be. Every day in the U.S., people make 35 million trips of 50–500 miles, stuck in traffic or routed through crowded hubs. Chances are, you've been one of them. At Electra, we're changing that with the EL9, a nine-passenger, hybrid-electric aircraft that takes off and lands in just 150 feet. Our Ultra Short technology opens up thousands of new places to fly, beyond conventional runways, congested airports and long drives. We're backed by Lockheed Martin, Honeywell and Safran. Operators worldwide have signed intent-to-purchase agreements for the first 2,200 aircraft we produce, and we're moving toward first test flights in 2027. 

Getting a new kind of aircraft airborne takes more than ambition. It takes our kind of bold: people who think big while working in the real world. Who move ideas into action and collaborate without silos. Who put people first and make room at the table for everyone. Who challenge one another without diminishing one another. 

Sound like you? Then look beyond what you thought were your own limits, and help us take flight beyond runways. 

The Role 

Electra.aero is seeking an experienced Senior Airspace Engineer to develop the methods, operational concepts, procedures, airspace solutions, and policies needed to safely integrate Ultra Short operations into the national airspace system, including at major airports and novel, distributed access points. 

The engineer will shape flight demonstrations, tabletop exercises, simulations, and data collection to inform Ultra Short policy, guidance, and standards development in the US and Europe. Collaboration with the FAA, NATCA, and industry standards development organizations is central to the role. 

This role requires a deep understanding of how aircraft performance, flight operations, airspace design, VFR/IFR procedures, PBN, RNAV/RNP operations, obstacle evaluation, navigation systems, FAA/EASA regulations, and real-world operational constraints intersect. The successful candidate will translate new aircraft capabilities and operational concepts into safe, certifiable, and operationally useful flight-path infrastructure. 

The ideal candidate understands airspace design and air traffic management concepts, tools, and workflows across congested terminal and en route airspace, and has led or contributed to research translating novel aircraft capabilities into operational procedures. They are comfortable working directly with the FAA, international civil aviation authorities, air navigation service providers, airport authorities, and local stakeholders to advance integration projects. Firsthand experience in procedure design, airspace design, or air traffic control is valuable; working familiarity with the FAA’s 8260-series Orders is expected. 

The engineer will collaborate with Electra and FAA teams through Electra’s Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA) with the FAA Tech Center, the FAA eIPP program, the Virginia Smart Airspace Program, and the International Test Arena in Norway, as well as through company-led testing and procedure development. 

What You’ll Do 

- Translate EL9 performance characteristics into Ultra Short operational capabilities, including ground footprint, obstacle clearance, and maneuvering. 

- Collaborate with aircraft performance engineers to model EL9 capabilities under normal, degraded, and contingency conditions, incorporating system safety analysis to define feasible Ultra Short procedures. 

- Develop candidate procedures for novel urban access points and existing airports, taking into account EL2/EL9 Ultra Short performance, instrument procedure design criteria, airport traffic flows, and the obstacle environment. 

- Review FAA, EASA, ICAO, and national standards—including fixed-wing, heliport, and vertiport frameworks, FAA 8260-series Orders, and international equivalents—to identify regulatory and policy gaps affecting proposed procedures. 

- Evaluate candidate procedures with Electra’s product team, the FAA, airport operations teams, and local air traffic control to prepare for flight demonstrations, tabletop exercises, simulations, and future policy and standards development. 

- Define learning objectives and data collection requirements for flight demonstrations and simulations to validate operational concepts. 

- Synthesize flight test results, lessons learned, and operational insights to inform regulatory workstreams developing Ultra Short policy and standards. 

- Support Electra’s commercial and infrastructure partnerships teams in assessing the feasibility of candidate access points in urban settings and at airports. 

- Develop thought leadership materials that clearly explain novel Ultra Short operational concepts to regulators, local stakeholders, and airport authorities. 

- Represent Electra in FAA, EASA, and ICAO working groups and industry standards development organizations to help shape standards, guidance, and policy for Ultra Short airspace integration and operations. 

What you Bring 

- Master’s degree or PhD in aerospace engineering, aviation management, airport planning, or a related field. 

- 5+ years of experience in airspace management research, policy and regulatory development, airspace or procedure design, or a related domain. 

- Strong working knowledge of FAA and/or EASA regulatory frameworks, including the AC 150 series, Part 135, Part 23, TERPS/PANS-OPS, 8260-series Orders, and relevant airport design standards. 

- Experience working with regulators, air navigation service providers, airport operators, and industry partners. 

- Strong technical writing and verbal communication skills. 

- Ability to thrive in a fast-moving, entrepreneurial environment with evolving requirements and limited precedent. 

Bonus Points 

- Experience leading or contributing to airspace integration research, including FAA, NASA, or MITRE airspace modernization initiatives. 

- Experience as an air traffic controller or with a non-FAA service provider specializing in instrument procedure design and development. 

- Private or commercial pilot experience. 

What We Offer 

- Medical, dental, and vision insurance; STD, LTD, and life insurance 

- Generous PTO, sick leave, and company holidays 

- Paid winter break 

- 401(k) with immediate vesting 

- Free catered lunches, coffee, snacks, and drinks at our Manassas headquarters 

- Free on-site parking 

Electra is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. This position may be subject to ITAR requirements.
