title: Senior Integration Software Engineer
description:
We are looking for an experienced Senior Integration Software Engineer to bring our algorithms and software backend together into reliable, operational solutions, and to take technical ownership of how our software is integrated.

Optics11 is a deep-tech company developing advanced fiber-optic sensing technologies for challenging environments and applications in energy and underwater security. Our systems enable high-performance sensing and monitoring through advanced photonics, signal processing, and data-driven intelligence.

We are expanding our R&D team with an Integration Software Engineer who enjoys building clean, reliable interfaces between components and working where software meets hardware, and who takes ownership of making complex systems work together end to end.

As a Senior Integration Software Engineer, you will support their integration into operational systems: connecting algorithms to the backend through robust APIs, building data connectors, health reporting and control software, and defining and verifying integrations with Command and Control (C2) systems.

You will work closely with domain experts in acoustics, signal processing and machine learning, and with the software engineering team, and hands-on with our monitoring systems at our headquarters and production facility. You will also take technical ownership of work delivered by internal and external engineers and set the standard for good engineering practices.

Key Responsibilities 

- Lead software integration engineering for our underwater acoustic sensing systems, ensuring frontend and backend components, algorithms, and hardware systems work together reliably.

- Integrate the algorithmic toolbox with our system backends, turning research code into maintainable, versioned and deployable software components.

- Implement data interfaces for our real-time sonar processing pipeline, to ingest multiple sensors (acoustic, heading, temperature, pressure, etc.) from internal and external data acquisition systems. Implement health reporting, logging and monitoring, so that the status and performance of software and system components is visible and actionable.

- Develop the software control layer for our sensing systems and their hardware components, including APIs for commanding, state handling, error handling and recovery.

- Implement, align and verify software integrations with external partners and C2 systems, being directly involved in defining interfaces, maintaining interface specifications and running joint integration tests.

- Testing & debugging: Develop system-level test suites and CI/CD pipelines, diagnose communication failures, and ensure secure, reliable data transfers as the toolbox and backends evolve.

- Address performance, latency and scalability of the integrated pipeline, together with algorithm and backend developers.

- Work hands-on with integrated software and hardware systems at our headquarters and production facility, with occasional on-site visits.

- Review the work of junior engineers and external development partners in depth, promote good practices for packaging, versioning and release, and share integration knowledge across the team.

Why Join Us? 

- Join one of Europe’s most promising deep-tech scale-ups.

- Shape the future of a rapidly growing multidisciplinary R&D organization.

- Competitive salary and benefits package.

- Enjoy regular team activities and company events.

- Fresh team lunches provided 5 times/week.

Qualifications:

- BSc or MSc in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related field.

- Significant professional experience in software engineering, with a focus on system integration, backend or platform development.

- Extensive experience developing production software in Python, including packaging, testing, dependency management and writing maintainable, well-structured code.

- Familiarity with systems programming in C++, or Rust, for the purpose of extending Python for more performance or hardware control.

- Proven experience designing and implementing APIs and messaging interfaces (e.g. MQTT, WebSocket) and data serialization (e.g. protobuf).

- Experience with realtime data pipelines, and handling high-throughput or streaming data.

- Experience with Docker, CI/CD and automated testing in a Linux environment.

- Experience working with software that interacts with physical systems, and comfort doing hands-on integration and troubleshooting in a lab or production environment.

- Experience reviewing code and designs, mentoring junior engineers, and setting engineering standards.

- An outcome-focused mindset, with the ability to own a problem end to end or break it down for others.

- Ability to work with algorithm developers and translate research code into robust, maintainable software.

- Flexible and proactive in taking on what needs to be addressed, and comfortable in a fast-paced scale-up environment.

- Good communication skills in English and the ability to coordinate with internal teams and external partners.

- Willingness to work primarily from our Amsterdam headquarters, as parts of the role involve classified information and physical systems.

Nice to Have:

- Knowledge of defense systems or defense standards (e.g. NATO STANAGs, MIL-STD), for example in naval, maritime security or surveillance systems.

- Experience with the scientific Python stack (e.g. NumPy, SciPy) or integrating signal processing or ML models into production systems.

- Experience developing software interfaces for controlling instruments or devices.

- Experience with other messaging or streaming frameworks (e.g. Kafka, ZeroMQ, DDS).

- Familiarity with observability tooling.

You'll be working with clients in the defense and security sectors, obtaining a Certificate of No Objection issued by the AIVD (Dutch General Intelligence and Security Service) is mandatory. title: Senior Business Controller (Operations)

You will be based at our head office in Almere. Hybrid working opportunities are limited: regular office attendance is important in this role because of the close collaboration with Finance, Operations and other stakeholders. You will also travel to the United Kingdom or Germany several times a year. 

About the role 

As Senior Business Controller, you will be responsible for business control within Operations and will also support our subsidiaries in the United Kingdom and Germany. You have a clear vision of what the best operational business control model looks like and have proven experience in realizing this. The Senior Business Controller plays a key role in strengthening financial control, transparency and decision-making across Operations. The scope covers procurement and product costing, as well as warehouse and transport operations. Working closely with Finance, Procurement and Operations, the Senior Business Controller translates operational developments and improvement initiatives into clear financial insights and P&L impact 

Our business is undergoing significant change. HG has recently changed its logistics service arrangements, consolidating most local warehouses into one central location as part of a cost-saving initiative. At the same time, a new ERP system is being implemented. This creates an interesting and dynamic environment in which existing budget models, cost allocation models, reporting and financial processes need to be further developed to reflect the new operating model and provide a solid basis for financial control and decision-making. 

What you will do 

Your responsibilities will include: 

- Owning the operational cost lines between Net Sales and Contribution Margin for the whole group and . act as a strong Finance business partner to the Chief Operating Officer and his team, translating operational developments into actionable financial insights; 

- Identifying and driving continuous improvements to the operational business, improving insights while reducing costs. 

- Being the financial business partner for the country managers in the UK and Germany, including reviewing commercial deals and business cases. 

- Analyzing budget versus actuals and explaining significant variances. 

- Developing a clear understanding of budgeted versus actual purchase prices and identifying the key drivers behind price variances. 

- Providing insight into raw material and purchase price developments and translating these into expected P&L impact. 

- Quantifying and tracking the financial impact of Procurement and product-costing initiatives and other savings programmes. 

- Establishing and further developing standard COGS based on expected cost developments. 

- Build a thorough understanding of the warehouse and distribution budget, operational performance and key savings initiatives. 

- Track whether the expected savings from the recently implemented warehouse and transport provider change are being realized in the P&L. 

- Further developing cost allocation models for individual markets, using meaningful drivers, and working towards more complete and reliable management reporting. 

- Ensuring the Operations P&L, budget and actual costs are consistently captured and reported in the same structure. 

- Translating inventory developments into financial impact and creating a clear link between stock levels, budget assumptions and cost allocation. 

- Supporting and improving an efficient month-end closing process, ensuring Operations costs are accurately and consistently booked, allocated and reconciled. 

- E stablish or improve proper accounting entries together with Finance Administration and relevant operational partners. 

- Co-lead the annual budget cycle and budget presentations to the Board. 

- Using and improving Power BI, ERP data and financial processes to reduce manual work and increase transparency. 

You will report directly to the Chief Financial Officer and work closely with colleagues in Finance, Procurement and Operations. You will also have regular contact with the Germany and UK country managers. 

This position requires more than strong analytical skills. You will need to explain your insights clearly, engage stakeholders and constructively challenge where necessary. You will be a knowledgeable sparring partner who asks questions, brings structure and takes responsibility from analysis through to implementation. You proactively identify opportunities to improve financial processes, controls, reporting and transparency across Operations. 

HG is a compact, fast-growing and international organization where you can directly see the impact of your work. This requires ownership, initiative and a pragmatic, results-oriented mindset. The team culture is open, pragmatic and focused on results, encouraging you to bring ideas forward, challenge constructively and take responsibility. Everything we do is guided by our three core values: Aim High, Be Brave, Be Connected. 

What you bring 

We are looking for a financially strong, hands-on and improvement-oriented controller who combines analytical capability with a practical understanding of Operations. The ideal candidate is comfortable working across Finance, Procurement and Operations and is able to turn complex cost drivers into clear insights and concrete actions. 

You bring a proactive mindset, strong stakeholder-management skills and a natural drive to simplify and improve processes. You are comfortable challenging existing ways of working, creating structure in a changing environment and taking ownership from analysis through implementation. 

You will also have: 

- A completed university master’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration or a related field. A Registered Controller (RC) qualification is a strong advantage. 

- Around 10 years of relevant experience in business control, operations control or a comparable financial role. 

- Experience in a manufacturing environment is important, including knowledge of production processes, procurement and cost calculations. 

- A sound understanding of business control, financial controls and treasury. 

- Experience with ERP systems and an understanding of how financial data and accounting flows are structured. 

- Good knowledge of Power BI. You do not need to build everything from scratch, but you can independently investigate, improve and develop analyses. 

- Experience working with consolidation tools. 

- Strong analytical, communication and stakeholder management skills. 

- A proactive, hands-on and improvement-oriented mindset, with the ability to create structure in a changing environment. 

- Fluency in English. Knowledge of Dutch is desirable, and German is an advantage. 

- Experience with AI tools, such as Copilot. 

- Willingness to travel to the United Kingdom and Germany several times a year. 

Please note that we do not offer visa or work permit sponsorship for this position. You must therefore hold a valid EU work permit 

What do we offer 

At HG, you will not be stepping into a role where everything is already set in stone. Changes in our logistics operations, systems and reporting create opportunities to further professionalize financial control and implement improvements yourself. 

You can expect: 

- a senior role with broad responsibility and direct influence on financial and operational decision-making; 

- a salary appropriate to the seniority of the role, with an indicative range of €85,000 to €100,000 gross per year; 

- an annual on-target bonus of 25% of your gross annual salary; 

- full-time employment with 30 days of annual leave;

- a full-time role based at our head office in Almere. Hybrid working is possible on a limited basis, with office attendance being an important part of the role;

- a friendly, welcoming team, with a free shared lunch every Monday and monthly social drinks. 

We are HG 

HG is a leading European brand in specialist cleaning and maintenance products. 

We believe a home should be a place where people can live carefree, with confidence in the products they use to care for the spaces and belongings around them. Our products are developed to do exactly what they promise: deliver effective, reliable and specialist cleaning solutions that help consumers solve real household problems. 

HG’s mission is to help people enjoy their homes without worrying about what might go wrong. We do this through high-quality products, specialist expertise, clear advice and a relentless focus on performance.

HG does what it promises.

description:

More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

How you'll make impact

You’ll help Airwallex manage and improve the economics of card payments, with a focus on scheme fees and interchange across Visa and Mastercard. You’ll turn complex network rules and payment data into accurate configurations, actionable analysis and decisions that improve cost visibility and margin performance.

- Own payment-cost analysis across scheme fees, interchange and network rules, identifying changes and translating them into clear financial, product and operational requirements.

- Maintain accurate fee tables, eligibility criteria and transaction-level logic with Product and Engineering, ensuring payment-cost calculations and customer billing reflect current network rules.

- Build models and reporting across markets, products, payment methods and transaction types to identify margin drivers, anomalies, leakage and opportunities to improve payment economics.

- Support cost and margin optimisation through transaction qualification, BIN routing, cost configuration and related levers, contributing to pricing, product design, market launches and commercial decisions.

- Strengthen governance, testing, reconciliation and controls by comparing expected costs with actual network charges and helping drive root-cause resolution.

- Partner with Finance, Product, Engineering, Data, Operations and external payment partners to resolve scheme pricing, interchange and rule-related questions.

You’ll work from our Amsterdam office three days a week.

What we're looking for

Essentials 

- Experience in payments, acquiring, issuing, card networks, payment infrastructure or a related role, ideally within a global PSP, acquirer, scheme, issuer or fintech.

- Strong knowledge of card payment economics, particularly Visa and Mastercard interchange, scheme fees, transaction qualification and network rules.

- Experience translating complex payment rules, fee schedules or network requirements into system logic, configurations and controls.

- Experience working with payment-cost systems or controls, including interchange tables, scheme fee logic, BIN-based rules, transaction attributes or similar payment configurations.

- Strong analytical and quantitative capabilities, including experience working with transaction-level data, economic modelling and reconciliation of expected versus actual payment costs.

title: Global Trainee Program - Outperformer Software Business Track (HILTI)
description:
4PS is part of the Hilti Group , which gives our people access to international opportunities and development programs within the wider Hilti organization. This vacancy is part of Hilti’s Global Trainee Program. Interested in joining the program? Please submit your application directly via Hilti Careerpage 

Construction technology is being reinvented. Be part of it.

Construction is one of the world's largest industries, and one of its least digitized. That is changing fast. At Hilti, we are not only developing software products - we are building and growing digital businesses around them. Hilti is at the centre of that shift, with a growing portfolio of software products that connect jobsites, offices, teams, and tools across the entire construction lifecycle. We are looking for ambitious, internationally mobile early-career talents with a global mindset who are excited about technology but see their future in business and leadership rather than in a purely technical software career.

The Software & Digital Business Track of Hilti's Outperformer Program is a two-year accelerated development program that prepares you for a commercial, international leadership career in our software and digital businesses. You will learn how technology becomes customer value, how software businesses grow, how products are brought to market, and how commercial decisions are made. This is not a rotation program where you shadow senior leaders. From day one, you carry real responsibility.

What You'll do

The Software Track is designed to build the next generation of software business leaders at Hilti – Business Owners, Business Directors, Segment Managers and ultimately Senior Management Team members. If you want a structured path to running a business, this program is built for that outcome.

The program places you inside one of two business units:

Construction Software: Home to Fieldwire (Field Software for project and workforce management), ON!Track (asset management), and 4PS (construction business management). You will work directly with customers, product teams, and business leadership across Europe and beyond.

Fastening & Protection Solutions: Where design & engineering software for structural connections (e.g. PROFIS Engineering Suite), MEP supports and passive fire protection systems are developed and brought to market across a global customer base of structural and mechanical engineers.

For the Construction Software business unit, the program is structured to provide a balanced foundation in customer and market exposure, software product understanding, and business experience, while giving you the opportunity to work with at least two software products during the program:

- ​Year 1: Begin with a 12-month sales assignment, developing direct customer insight and understanding the business challenges addressed by our software solutions.

- ​Year 2: Undertake three rotations of 3–6 months each across product and business teams, including exposure to an international project.

​For the Fastening & Protection Solution business unit, the program provides exposure to product management , software development, exposure to customers and start-ups and international project experience:

- ​Year 1: Begin with a 12-month product management assignment, building product understanding and market insight.

- ​Year 2: Undertake three rotations of 3–6 months each, involving international projects that broaden your business perspective and global exposure.

You will have a dedicated senior mentor from the start, direct exposure to executive leadership, and a peer cohort of Global Trainees across all Hilti business tracks globally.

What You’ll Bring

You are close to graduating or have recently completed a Master's degree - your degree is likely to be in construction management, civil engineering, or mechanical engineering with a focus on construction, Computer Science, or also Business study programs with an affinity for Software and construction. What matters more than your degree subject is the combination of traits below:

- Global mobility - you are willing and able to relocate internationally, multiple times. A global thinker who is keen for diverse cultural experiences.

- Digital and AI orientation - you think natively in digital workflows, comfortable with software tools, and know the power and potential of AI.

- Language - you are fluent in English and/or German, Dutch, French, Spanish or Italian. 

- Commercial instinct - you are drawn to how businesses grow, how customers make decisions, and how products create.

- Low ego, high drive - you take the work seriously and yourself lightly. You seek feedback, move fast, and are energised by ambiguity rather than unsettled by it.

- You are at the start of your career and have maximum three years of junior work experience.

What’s In It for You

​​Show us what you can do, and in return, we promise you the experience of a lifetime. We offer you a transformative journey filled with learning, growth, and invaluable experiences that will shape your perspective and personal and professional development. On top of that, you’ll also take part in some fascinating courses and events:

- Introductory Global Summit: Experience 4 days at our global headquarters in Liechtenstein, featuring the presence of our Executive Board and Global Senior Leadership. The summit offers a comprehensive overview of our business, while fostering soft skill development and meaningful collaboration with fellow program participants.

- Social Project Summit: 7 days dedicated to building a better future, with contribution to a hands-on, high-impact community project. This experience offers the chance to immerse yourself in a different culture while actively improving living conditions for those in need.

- Leadership Summit: An enriching learning journey in partnership with a renowned business school, featuring online modules and collaborative projects with fellow program participants. The experience concludes with a 5-day on-campus summit to deepen insights and to foster business and leadership skills.

Why Hilti

Hilti is a global leader in construction innovation, with more than 34,000 team members across 120 countries. Guided by our purpose, Making Construction Better, we’re driven to keep learning, growing, and finding new ways to make a lasting impact. Here, you’ll be empowered to use your strengths, work with a global and inclusive team, and take on meaningful challenges. At Hilti, you’ll have the chance to make your ideas, achievements, and growth real through purpose, passion, and teamwork.

Learn more about our recruitment process: https://careers.hilti.group/en/candidate-interview-preparation/

Commitment to Inclusion

​​At Hilti, inclusion is a key focus in how we work, lead, and grow together. We are committed to embracing diversity of thought and creating an environment that is inclusive of everyone, everywhere. We continuously strive to ensure every voice is valued and every team member feels empowered to contribute. By building on this foundation, we strengthen our teams, our innovation, and our impact, making construction better together.

​Exciting software journey: You will dive into the fast-paced world of our construction software business, gaining exposure to innovative digital solutions that are transforming one of the world's largest industries.
​
​Global cross-team collaboration: You will work with colleagues worldwide and get guidance from a dedicated mentor as you grow in your career.

​We hire for a career, not for a position. If you are looking for long-term career prospects and opportunities to grow, this is the perfect start.​

​Are you ready to jumpstart your career? Our hiring process is designed to help you showcase your skills and experience. The process has multiple steps and requires a longer period of time:

- It all starts with your application and a video interview.

- Get connected with our HR team in an online interview.

- Get ready to flex your problem-solving muscles with our online Business Case Round.

- Impress our Business Line Managers with your presentation skills and insights during the next round.

- And, if you make it to the end, you'll receive an invitation to our Assessment Center.

​Exciting, right? Let's get started!

4PS is part of the Hilti Group , which gives our people access to international opportunities and development programs within the wider Hilti organization. This vacancy is part of Hilti’s Global Trainee Program. Interested in joining the program? Please submit your application directly via Hilti Careerpage .

​The Assessment Center will take place in Liechtenstein at Hilti Headquarter on December 1st and 2nd, 2026. Applications will be reviewed in the order they’re received, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible since there are limited spots for the Assessment Center!​

Als AI Engineer werk je in een klein en gedreven team aan de ontwikkeling van AivyCare. Je schakelt direct met engineering, architectuur, product en domeinkennis. Wij zoeken niet primair op senioriteit of een vast aantal jaren ervaring. Voor ons zijn mindset, eigenaarschap en het vermogen om mee te bouwen in een ondernemende omgeving belangrijker. title: Senior Legal Counsel - Product & AI (Part-time)
description:
Amsterdam (hybrid) | Part-time (freelance) 8 hours a week | €2,000 to €2,500 per month 

Foleon is a leading content creation platform providing business teams with a fast and scalable way to produce highly-engaging content experiences that bring a new level of intelligence to their customer journeys. 

Foleon is based in Amsterdam and New York and serves more than 1,200 global B2B brands. We value people who are bold, ambitious, collaborative, and customer-centric. Even better, the ones who know how to work hard and have fun at the same time. We’re a team of highly driven people, with a great sense of human connection and a clear focus. 

Your Mission 

As our Senior Product & AI Counsel, you’ll own the legal side of our product and AI proposition, working with us about one day a week on a retainer basis. It’s a new role. You’ll work closely with Product, Engineering and leadership to make sure what we build and ship holds up under the EU AI Act, cybersecurity law, digital accessibility rules and GDPR.

Your Job 

- Act as our product counsel: join product syncs, review features before they’re built, and flag legal and compliance questions early.

- Lead compliance for our AI proposition: classify our AI use cases, map our obligations as a provider or deployer under the EU AI Act, and set up the documentation, transparency and governance it requires.

- Make sure our platform, and the content our customers publish with it, meets the European Accessibility Act and related standards.

- Build privacy into the product by advising on GDPR questions tied to new features and data.

- Advise on cybersecurity law, including NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act and incident reporting duties, working closely with our security team.

- Track changes in AI, cybersecurity, accessibility and privacy regulation, and turn them into practical guidance for the team.

Your Competencies & Skills 

- Senior and independent: you make calls and own them, without someone steering you.

- A practical communicator who explains complex regulation to product teams in plain language, with answers instead of memos full of caveats.

- Proactive and curious: you spot gaps before they become problems and want to understand how the product actually works.

- Comfortable working part-time and flexibly, and available when something urgent comes up.

Your Qualifications 

- A Master’s in Law (or equivalent) and 6+ years of experience, ideally a mix of law firm and in-house at a tech or SaaS company.

- Hands-on experience as product counsel for software, ideally including AI products.

- Deep working knowledge of the EU AI Act and how it applies to AI propositions in practice.

- Experience with cybersecurity law (NIS2, Cyber Resilience Act) and digital accessibility rules (European Accessibility Act).

- A solid grounding in commercial and corporate law, with working knowledge of employment law.

- GDPR and privacy expertise is a plus, ideally at DPO level or with a certification such as CIPP/E.

- Experience working with scale-ups on a retainer or fractional basis is a plus.

- Fluent English. Dutch is a plus.

Note: All our hiring is done in-house, so we’re not looking for agency support for this role. Thanks for understanding!

Aufgaben

- Kickoff: Du führst Kickoff-Calls per Video mit neuen Kunden und klärst, wie die Prozesse, die wir für sie automatisieren aussehen.

- Tempo: Nach der Einarbeitung betreust du mehrere Setups parallel und startest bis zu einen neuen Kunden pro Tag.

So arbeiten wir dich ein

- Woche 1: Du lernst unsere Abläufe, unser Studio und den Setup-Standard kennen und baust deinen eigenen KI-Agenten, falls du noch keinen hast (inkl. aller relevanten Schulungen).

- Woche 2: Du bist bei Kickoff-Calls und Setups unseres Technik-Teams dabei.

- Ab Woche 3: Du führst deinen ersten eigenen Kickoff, und hast einen Mentor an deiner Seite, der dich dabei unterstützt.

- Nach rund 4 Wochen: Du machst Calls, Setup und Support eigenständig und übernimmst nach und nach immer mehr Eigenverantwortung.

Qualifikation

title: Community Manager Schulen (m/w/d)
description:
Deine Rolle

Du sorgst dafür, dass neue Schulen teech kennenlernen und bestehende Schulen sich bei uns gut aufgehoben fühlen. Dafür entwickelst du unser Schulnetzwerk eigenverantwortlich weiter, baust verlässliche Beziehungen zu Lehrkräften und Ansprechpartnern auf und begleitest Schulen bei der Nutzung unserer Bildungsformate.

Du behältst den gesamten Weg im Blick: vom ersten Kontakt über die erste Teilnahme bis zur regelmäßigen Nutzung im Unterricht. Gemeinsam mit der Geschäftsführung vereinbarst du konkrete Ziele und KPIs, steuerst deine Aktivitäten danach und berichtest regelmäßig über Fortschritte, Ergebnisse und Handlungsbedarf. Dabei arbeitest du eng mit dem gesamten teech-Team zusammen.

Deine Aufgaben

Neue Schulen identifizieren und gewinnen

- Du recherchierst relevante Schulen und passende Ansprechpartner, priorisierst Potenziale und entwickelst unser Schulnetzwerk systematisch weiter.
- Du stellst aktiv den Erstkontakt her - telefonisch, per E-Mail und über passende weitere Kontaktwege.
- Du vermittelst den Nutzen unserer Angebote für Schule und Unterricht, fasst konsequent nach und gewinnst Schulen für die Teilnahme an unseren Formaten.
Schulen betreuen und Beziehungen ausbauen

- Du bist ein verlässlicher Ansprechpartner für unsere Schulen und pflegst den regelmäßigen Austausch.
- Du begleitest neue Schulen beim Einstieg, beantwortest Fragen und unterstützt sie dabei, passende Angebote für ihren Unterricht zu finden.
- Du informierst gezielt über neue Formate, Veranstaltungen und Teilnahmemöglichkeiten.
- Du erkennst, wenn Schulen Unterstützung brauchen oder länger nicht aktiv waren, und gehst auf sie zu.
- Du holst Feedback ein und bringst die Bedürfnisse der Schulen strukturiert ins Team ein.
Eigenverantwortlich steuern und Ergebnisse sichtbar machen

- Du organisierst deinen Bereich selbstständig und dokumentierst Kontakte, Aktivitäten und nächste Schritte nachvollziehbar.
- Du arbeitest mit vereinbarten KPIs, beispielsweise zu neu gewonnenen Schulen, aktiven Schulen, Teilnahmen und wiederkehrender Nutzung.
- Du erstellst regelmäßige Reportings für die Geschäftsführung, ordnest Ergebnisse ein und leitest konkrete Maßnahmen ab.
- Du entwickelst Abläufe für Ansprache und Betreuung weiter und nutzt digitale Werkzeuge, um wiederkehrende Aufgaben effizienter zu gestalten.
Im gesamten Team zusammenarbeiten

- Du stimmst dich eng mit Projektmanagement, Sales, Marketing und Produktverantwortlichen ab.
- Du verbindest die Bedürfnisse der Schulen mit unseren Angeboten und laufenden Projekten.
- Ergänzend erstellst du zielgruppengerechte Einladungen, E-Mails und Newsletter und unterstützt bei Inhalten für Website, Plattform und Social Media. Der Schwerpunkt deiner Rolle bleibt die Gewinnung und Betreuung der Schulen.
Das bringst du mit

- Du hast Freude daran, Menschen anzusprechen, Beziehungen aufzubauen und diese langfristig zu pflegen.
- Du kommunizierst klar, freundlich und verbindlich - auch am Telefon.
- Du arbeitest eigenverantwortlich, setzt Prioritäten und bleibst an vereinbarten nächsten Schritten dran.
- Du denkst in Zielen und Ergebnissen und kannst Kennzahlen auswerten und verständlich aufbereiten.
- Du verstehst die Bedürfnisse von Schulen und Lehrkräften oder hast Lust, dich intensiv damit auseinanderzusetzen.
- Du arbeitest gerne im Team und bringst Informationen und Ideen aktiv ein.
- Du gehst sicher mit digitalen Werkzeugen um und bist offen für neue Arbeitsweisen.
- Erfahrung in Schulbetreuung, Community Management, Kundenbetreuung oder Vertrieb ist hilfreich.
- Du kannst Inhalte verständlich und zielgruppengerecht formulieren.
So arbeiten wir

Wir setzen KI gezielt als Assistenz im Arbeitsalltag ein - etwa bei Recherche, Vorbereitung, Auswertung und wiederkehrenden Aufgaben. Damit verbessern wir unsere Prozesse und schaffen mehr Zeit für das Wesentliche: persönliche Betreuung, verlässliche Zusammenarbeit und gute Ergebnisse.

Dabei behalten wir den gesamten Ablauf im Blick: Wie greifen einzelne Schritte ineinander? Wo stockt es? Wo müssen wir gezielt eingreifen? Du bringst Ideen ein, hinterfragst bestehende Abläufe und nutzt digitale Werkzeuge und KI, um unsere Arbeit sinnvoll zu vereinfachen. Dein Urteilsvermögen und der persönliche Kontakt bleiben dabei entscheidend.

Das bieten wir dir

- Eine sinnstiftende Aufgabe mit direktem Einfluss auf die Zusammenarbeit mit Schulen und die Bildungsangebote für junge Menschen.
- Viel Gestaltungsspielraum und Verantwortung für einen eigenen Bereich.
- Eine Stelle in Vollzeit oder Teilzeit.
- Ein engagiertes Team und kurze Wege zur Geschäftsführung.
- Flexible Arbeitszeiten und hybride Zusammenarbeit.
- Dein Arbeitsort ist schwerpunktmäßig Darmstadt. Du bist bereit, auch im Office zu arbeiten. Die konkrete Aufteilung zwischen Büro und mobilem Arbeiten sowie individuelle Regelungen stimmen wir gemeinsam ab.
- Einblicke in unser Netzwerk aus Bildung, Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft.
Über teech

teech verbindet Unternehmen, Schulen und junge Menschen. Mit digitalen Bildungsformaten und ClassChats ermöglichen wir Schülern den direkten Austausch mit Persönlichkeiten aus Wirtschaft, Wissenschaft und Gesellschaft. Gemeinsam mit unseren Partnern machen wir Berufsorientierung greifbar und eröffnen neue Perspektiven für die Zukunft.

Deine Bewerbung

Du möchtest unser Schulnetzwerk weiterentwickeln und dafür sorgen, dass Schulen gerne und regelmäßig mit teech zusammenarbeiten? Deine Ansprechpartnerin ist Sarah Monaco.

title: Forschungsprojektleiter:in Energiedaten & Gebäudetechnik (d/w/m)
description:
termios macht Heizen in Wohn- und Gewerbeimmobilien smarter und klimafreundlicher. Unser Thermostat spart spürbar Energie und hilft Asset Managern, Wohnungsunternehmen und Eigentümern, ihre ESG- und Net-Zero-Ziele zu erreichen.

termios ist ein 2023 gegründetes Joint-Venture von mantro als Company Builder, dem sauerländischen Familienunternehmen Oventrop und der Düsseldorfer LEG Immobilien SE. Als Technologieunternehmen entwickeln wir grüne Lösungen rund um Heizen, Nachhaltigkeit und ESG für Wohnimmobilien.

Warum wir diese Stelle besetzen 

Unser Thermostat termios Pro übernimmt den hydraulischen Abgleich automatisch, für jeden einzelnen Heizkörper, und ist in tausenden Wohnungen verbaut. Daraus entsteht ein Messdatenbestand zum realen Heizbetrieb im Gebäudebestand, wie ihn kaum ein einzelnes Forschungsprojekt aufbauen kann.

Wie viel Energie spart der automatische Abgleich wirklich, unter welchen Bedingungen, und wie weist man das sauber nach? Diese und ähnliche Fragestellungen wollen wir gemeinsam mit Hochschulen, Forschungsinstituten, Wohnungsunternehmen und Fördergebern beantworten.

Du startest dabei nicht bei null: Wir haben bereits zwei vom BMWE geförderte Forschungsprojekte und sind in weiteren Forschungsfeldern aktiv. Für dieses wachsende Portfolio suchen wir zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt jemanden, der Forschung nicht nur organisiert, sondern selbst betreibt.

Deine Aufgaben

- Studiendesign und Feldversuche: Du übersetzt offene Fragen in prüfbare Hypothesen und ein belastbares Studiendesign mit Vergleichsgruppen, Baseline, Witterungsbereinigung und Messkonzept. Messkampagnen in realen Liegenschaften setzt du gemeinsam mit Field Service und Anlagentechnik um.

- Datenanalyse: Du wertest Zeitreihen aus dem Gerätebestand und aus Messkampagnen selbst aus, quantifizierst Effekte und Unsicherheiten und trennst sauber zwischen Korrelation und Wirkung.

- Ergebnisse: Du bereitest Erkenntnisse für Abschlussberichte, Fachpublikationen, Konferenzen und Kunden auf und sorgst dafür, dass sie in unsere Algorithmen und Produktentwicklung zurückfließen.

- Projektleitung: Du steuerst mehrere parallel laufende Forschungs- und Pilotprojekte, von Arbeitspaketen und Meilensteinen über Budgets und Berichtspflichten bis zu Kooperationsverträgen, Datenschutz und Förderrichtlinien.

- Förderung und Akquise: Du findest passende Förderprogramme auf Landes-, Bundes- und EU-Ebene, entwickelst Projektideen mit Partnern und schreibst Skizzen und Anträge.

Das bringst du mit

- Studium: Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium in einem ingenieur-, natur- oder datenwissenschaftlichen Fach, z. B. Gebäude- und Energietechnik, Versorgungstechnik, Bauphysik, Physik, Mathematik oder Informatik.

- Forschungserfahrung: Du hast mehrere Jahre in der angewandten Forschung gearbeitet, etwa an einem Fraunhofer-Institut, einer anderen Forschungseinrichtung, einer Hochschule oder in einer F&E-Abteilung, idealerweise im Umfeld Gebäude, Energie oder TGA.

- Methodik und Daten: Du hast Studien oder Messkampagnen selbst konzipiert und ausgewertet, wendest statistische Verfahren wie Regression, Zeitreihenanalyse und Hypothesentests sicher an und arbeitest dabei mit Python oder R sowie SQL.

- Projektleitung: Du hast Projekte mit mehreren Partnern geleitet oder koordiniert und bringst unterschiedliche Interessen zusammen.

- Kommunikation: Du schreibst klar und belastbar, vom Förderantrag bis zur Veröffentlichung. Du sprichst verhandlungssicher Deutsch und Englisch auf Arbeitsniveau.

Das ist ein Plus

Niemand bringt alles mit. Vieles davon lernst du bei uns.

- Förderprojekte: Du hast schon Anträge geschrieben oder öffentlich geförderte Projekte abgewickelt.

- Heizungstechnik: Du kennst dich mit Heizungshydraulik, hydraulischem Abgleich und Wärmeerzeugern wie Fernwärme oder Wärmepumpe aus.

- Einsparnachweise: Du kennst Verfahren zur Messung und Verifikation von Einsparungen, z. B. IPMVP.

- Modelle: Du hast Erfahrung mit Gebäudesimulation (z. B. Modelica, TRNSYS) oder Machine Learning.

- Promotion oder eigene Publikationen 

Gute Gründe, um bei uns durchzustarten

- Forschung, die ankommt: Wenn du eine Hypothese an einem realen Gebäude prüfen willst, organisieren wir das. Was du herausfindest, landet im Produkt, und Veröffentlichungen sind ausdrücklich erwünscht.

- Alles unter einem Dach: Hardware, Firmware, Funk, Cloud und Daten. Wer das gebaut hat, wonach du fragst, sitzt im selben Team.

- Gestaltungsfreiraum ab dem ersten Tag, in einem agilen Team mit flachen Hierarchien und kurzen Entscheidungswegen.

- Flexibilität: Du arbeitest hybrid in Düsseldorf oder München, mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten.

- Konditionen: Unbefristete Festanstellung, wettbewerbsfähige Vergütung, 30 Tage Urlaub, Urban Sports und Corporate Benefits sowie regelmäßige Teamevents.

Klingt nach dir?

Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung mit Lebenslauf, gern mit Publikationsliste oder Links zu deinen Projekten. Ein Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht. Schreib uns lieber ein paar Sätze dazu, welche Forschungsfrage dich bei uns besonders reizt.

title: Senior Privacy Counsel (m/f/d)
description:
Deep Blue Recruitment is working with an international technology company looking to appoint an experienced Senior Privacy Counsel to join its legal team.

Operating in the enterprise technology sector, the business develops software and digital solutions for customers across a range of industries. With continued investment in emerging technologies, including AI, data protection is becoming an increasingly important consideration in how the business develops its products, manages risk and works with customers.

We're looking for a commercially minded privacy lawyer who enjoys working closely with the business, understanding how technology works and finding practical solutions to complex legal questions.

This is a broad, hands-on role combining privacy advisory work, commercial support and the continued development of internal data protection processes.

What You'll Be Doing

- Advise colleagues across the business on a broad range of privacy and data protection matters, providing clear, commercially focused legal guidance.
- Work closely with product, technology and commercial teams on the development of new services, ensuring privacy considerations are addressed early in the process.
- Support the negotiation of commercial agreements, particularly around data processing, international transfers, customer relationships and third-party arrangements.
- Advise on GDPR and other applicable international data protection regulations, helping the business understand and manage its obligations across different markets.
- Provide legal guidance on emerging technologies, including AI, and the implications of new products and data processing activities from a privacy perspective.
- Review and improve existing privacy policies, internal procedures and governance frameworks to ensure they remain practical and fit for purpose.
- Work alongside information security and IT teams on data governance, risk assessments and privacy-related incidents.
- Identify opportunities to improve the efficiency of privacy operations, including through automation and better internal processes.
- Monitor regulatory developments affecting technology businesses, particularly around data protection, AI and digital services.
- Provide training and guidance to colleagues across the organisation, helping non-legal teams understand their responsibilities when handling personal data.
What They're Looking For

- A qualified lawyer with approximately 4-8 years experience specialising in data protection, privacy or technology law, gained in private practice, in-house or a combination of both.
- Strong knowledge of GDPR and European data protection law, including regulatory guidance and its practical application within commercial organisations.
- Experience advising technology businesses, ideally with exposure to software, AI, digital products or other data-intensive environments.
- A good understanding of artificial intelligence technologies and the legal and regulatory challenges associated with their development and use.
- Experience advising on commercial agreements involving personal data, international transfers and complex data processing arrangements.
- Comfortable working directly with product, engineering and technical stakeholders, with the ability to understand complex issues and provide clear, practical legal advice.
- A commercial approach to risk management, recognising that the role of legal is to help the business find workable solutions rather than simply identify problems.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities independently.
- Experience working within an international business or advising on privacy matters across multiple jurisdictions would be beneficial.
Why Consider This Opportunity?

This is an opportunity to join an international technology business where privacy plays an important role in how the company operates, develops its products and works with customers.

You'll have a broad remit, working closely with different teams across the organisation on a range of commercial, operational and regulatory matters, including some of the challenges emerging technologies bring to data protection.

If you're a privacy lawyer who enjoys working closely with the business, has an interest in technology and takes a practical approach to solving legal challenges, we'd be interested in hearing from you.

Integrationen sind das, was diesem Motor echte Power gibt: die Daten, Tools und Systeme, die aus einem cleveren AI-Agenten einen machen, der Prozesse wirklich automatisiert und Probleme löst. 

Gegründet im Jahr 2020, ist Superchat heute die Plattform für über 10.000 Unternehmen weltweit - von bekannten Marken wie Allianz, Auto1, Enpal, Danone und GASAG bis hin zu kleinen Unternehmen, Zahnarztpraxen und Solo-Founder:innen, die professioneller auftreten möchten.

Inzwischen laufen täglich Millionen von Nachrichten über Superchat.

Gestartet sind wir als Unified Inbox - ein zentraler Ort für alle Kommunikationskanäle wie WhatsApp, E-Mail, SMS oder Instagram. Mit dem Aufstieg von ChatGPT begann unser nächstes Kapitel: AI Agents, die über Chat, E-Mail und Voice in einer Qualität kommunizieren, die mit den besten menschlichen Teams mithalten kann.

Heute sind wir ein Team von rund 100 Mitarbeitenden , arbeiten profitabel und haben insgesamt 18 Millionen Euro Funding eingesammelt (unsere letzte Finanzierungsrunde liegt bereits 4,5 Jahre zurück - seitdem wachsen wir aus eigener Kraft weiter).

Unser Hauptsitz ist in Berlin. 

Als Werkstudent:in im Customer Support bist du die erste Anlaufstelle für unsere Kund:innen. - Wir glauben an Zusammenarbeit vor Ort: Wir sind gerne gemeinsam im Berliner Office. title: Robot Learning Engineer
description:
Why this role is exciting 

Rohlik is the leading Central European e-grocer. More than a million customers buy their groceries from us through Rohlik.cz , Knuspr.de , Kifli.hu , Gurkerl.at and Sezamo.ro , choosing from over 17,000 items, delivered within a couple of hours in 15-minute windows.

We are building the autonomous grocer. Maia, our AI assistant, already talks to customers and builds their orders; agents are moving into our buying and logistics; vision models are learning to watch quality. The next frontier is physical: robots taking over more and more of the work in our fulfilment centres, until fresh food moves from producers to households at a cost nobody else can match.

We are setting out to record how our own people handle groceries and to turn those recordings into a training corpus for manipulation policies. Our warehouses already log what happened on every pick and every quality check, so the recordings can carry labels most datasets never get. Making that hold is part of the job.

You decide what makes an hour of footage trainable — before we bank hundreds of them. 

What you will own and deliver 

- The capture spec. Cameras, mounts, calibration, and what disqualifies an episode. You write it before we buy the fleet and enforce it after. When the spec and the floor disagree, you go to the floor and find out which one is wrong.

- Ground truth. Hand pose is the signal that transfers from human video to robot policies, and warehouse reality — work gloves, occlusion, cold halls — is exactly where the published models struggle. You own how we measure that and how we close the gap.

- The evaluation harness. The corpus only counts if a policy can train on it. You build the harness that decides which hours make the bank, and you hold the trainability bar as the volume grows.

- The first training runs. Once hours bank, you post-train open robot-learning models on our data and run the first task evaluations.

- Judgment before spend. The field moves monthly. You read what is published, reproduce the claims we depend on, and steer our capture before the money is spent, not after.

The scope 

This is a seat on a small, newly created team: an operations lead who runs capture on the floor, a data engineer who owns the pipeline, and you: the machine-learning voice in the room. This is not a research-scientist role, and no publication record is required. The job is to make a corpus trainable and to train the first policies on it.

What we are looking for 

- 3+ years of relevant full-time robotics experience.

- PyTorch, and computer vision with real 3D geometry. Camera calibration, pose estimation, SLAM fundamentals. You have debugged an extrinsic calibration at least once in your life and know why it drifted.

- You can read a paper and reproduce it. Our pipeline is assembled from published work, and your job is knowing which claims survive contact with a chilled warehouse hall.

- You know what policies train on. Familiar with the current robot-learning stack and policy classes well enough to know what the training side will demand of the data before the data exists.

- Dataset instincts. You have trained on data you collected yourself, and you know the failure modes that only show up at training tim..

- Comfortable as the only ML voice. You make the call, write it down, and revisit it when the pilot data says otherwise.

- AI is how work gets done here. Our engineers use Claude Code and Devin daily, and we expect you to direct agents for the unglamorous parts — harness code, data plumbing, reproduction scripts — while keeping the quality bar exactly where it was.

- Particularly relevant. Hand-pose estimation or egocentric video in production; multi-camera rigs and time sync; experience post-training robot-learning models; ROS 2.

What success looks like in 90 days 

You have written the capture spec and we set up the first rigs against it. Your pilot gates have numbers, the first hours have passed your harness, and you can tell the people who sign the budget, with data, what the next hundred hours should look like.

Are we a good fit? 

Take this role if you would rather own the spec that decides whether a dataset becomes an asset or a write-off than tune someone else's model on someone else's data, if a fulfilment centre at 6 a.m. sounds like a lab to you, and if you want the shortest possible line between your technical judgment and a capital decision. Read our culture code and are we a good fit? .

What we offer 

- The physical-AI side of the autonomous grocer, with the capture spec and the first training runs yours from day one

- A data asset few teams in the world get to build, in fresh groceries, a domain as hard as manipulation gets

- Off-the-shelf hardware, a managed cloud estate, and a mandate that has already started

- Benefits — see what we offer 

Are you in? 

Instead of a cover letter: pick a published human-video-to-robot-policy pipeline you rate, and tell us where it breaks on a warehouse floor where every hand wears a work glove.

#LI-ML1 #Knuspr

title: Head of Finance Automation/ AI Agentification
description:
Finance at Rohlik is being rebuilt to run on AI. We already have agents in production that chase overdue payments, process invoices, allocate cash and clear the team's inbox. The pieces work. What we need now is one person to own the whole thing and make it deliver at scale.

Role Overview 

This is a new role that owns how AI and automation reshape the finance operating model across the Group. You will take a programme that is already live across procure to pay, order to cash and our shared services centre, and turn it from a set of promising experiments into the way finance actually runs.

You report to the Group CFO. You inherit a small team and a live roadmap, and you own the result. You decide what gets automated first, you build and ship with AI tools when that is the fastest way, and you hold every workstream to a number.

The role is deliberately hands on . You should be close enough to the work to build an agent or connect two systems through an API with AI assistance, even though you are not a software developer. You should also be senior enough to redesign how finance works and bring the rest of the business with you.

Why this role is exciting 

- You’ll inherit a live AI programme with real agents, real data and real impact from day one — not a greenfield slide deck.

- You’ll shape how Finance actually runs across the Group as we move toward the next stage of growth — including the journey toward IPO readiness.

- You’ll have access to a top-notch AI-first tech stack and the freedom to use it pragmatically.

- You’ll work directly with the Group CFO , with fast decisions and no corporate red tape.

- Your good ideas will be implemented almost immediately — not parked in a roadmap waiting for HQ approval.

- You’ll lead a small team, but this is not a “manager from a distance” role. It’s highly hands-on , high-impact, and built for someone who wants to make things move fast.

What we expect from you 

- Own the AI and automation agenda across finance, from strategy through delivery to measured impact.

- Lead process redesign the right way: map and understand the as-is, then design an agentic-first to-be rather than automating the old steps. 

- Lead complex cross-functional programmes across Finance, Tech and Operations, driving delivery through stakeholders and teams beyond your direct reporting line.

- Bring the live programme to its targets, with a clear owner, baseline and deadline behind every workstream.

- Redesign core finance processes around AI and agents, starting with close, reporting and forecasting.

- Build and ship yourself when it is faster, using AI assisted tools to create agents and connect systems such as NetSuite, Rossum and n8n.

- Lead and grow the team (three today) and raise AI fluency across finance and the SSC so the business can use what you build.

- Track what matters and report it straight: automation rate, close time, cash allocation speed, cost and effort taken out.

- Roll out across our five markets, balancing local reality against one Group standard.

What we look for 

You have probably spent time in strategy consulting or in a transformation role, and you are now genuinely excited by what AI can do. You are a sharp generalist who can walk into a messy process, find the real problem, and fix it. You are as comfortable in a CFO pre-read as you are in the AI first tool building the thing.

- A track record of leading transformation or automation programmes that actually delivered. A consulting, operations or generalist operator background all fit.

- Strong understanding of finance processes , ideally gained through finance transformation, operating model redesign or automation programmes.

- Hands on with AI . You can build agents and integrate APIs with AI assistance. You are not a software engineer and you do not need to be, but the tooling does not scare you.

- You set baselines, name owners, hit deadlines, and say so early when something slips.

- You can lead a small team and still do the work yourself.

- You prioritise by impact and move fast. Better done than perfect.

- You bring finance, tech and operations along with you.

- Fluent in English. other languages will be an advantage.

- Regular travel to Prague HQ required (min. 4 days per month)

What we offer

- Knuspr Xtra account and 10% discount in the form of Knuspr credits / cashback

description:

Turn board design insight into reliable tests that detect manufacturing defects in Graphcore’s hardware.

As a Senior Board Test Engineer in Bristol, you’ll develop manufacturing tests for Graphcore’s advanced electronic products. You’ll focus on printed circuit board assemblies and the faults that affect their operation.

Your work will help improve defect coverage across the test and inspection tools used by contract electronics manufacturers. You’ll help the team detect and manage hardware faults arising during manufacturing and product use.

You’ll analyse PCB designs for testability and manufacturing risks, then develop boundary scan and embedded functional tests. You’ll also diagnose complex electronic faults down to component level.

Leading firms like BCLP, Orrick, Goodwin, Womble Bond Dickinson and Clifford Chance rely on Orbital to remove the busywork, freeing legal and real estate teams to focus on sharp judgment, standout client service, and closing deals faster.

💡 Working at Orbital means joining a bold, ambitious team, with the trust to take ownership and make a real impact from day one.

Role Overview 🔎

We're looking for a Product Security Engineer to own the security of Orbital's product: the AI agent our customers use, the platform it runs on, and how we build both.

Our customers are law firms and real estate businesses. They trust us with confidential transaction documents, and they ask hard questions about how we protect them. Our product is an AI agent that reads those documents, calls tools and runs code on a lawyer's behalf. That brings the usual cloud security work and a newer set of risks: prompt injection, agents acting on untrusted input, and attackers using AI to move faster than before.

You'll be our first in-house product security engineer, taking on work we have so far relied on contractors for. You'll build security into the product rather than review it from outside: you'll decide how we rate a vulnerability and how fast we act on it, build the automated systems that find and fix issues before an attacker does, and set the security bar that engineering builds to. You'll work alongside our product engineers, with the authority to require changes across teams on security grounds, independent of any one team's delivery deadlines. An information security lead will own company-wide policy, compliance and customer assurance, and you'll work closely with them.

You won't start from zero. Our AWS environment follows the Well-Architected Framework, with GuardDuty, Security Hub, encryption at rest and scoped credentials in place, and we hold SOC 2 and ISO 27001 commitments to our customers. What we need is someone to own it, find the gaps, and raise the standard as the company and the threat landscape grow.

You'll get a chance to 👩‍💻 👨‍💻

- Build an automated security harness. Put agents to work on our product: continuous red-team and blue-team loops that probe the agent, the platform and our code, find vulnerabilities, and propose or ship the fix. Manual review should be justified when required and automatic harness improvement is expected.

- Own vulnerability management end to end. Define how we classify severity and the response time each level demands, so a critical CVE gets fixed the same day. Automate patching, dependency and image scanning, and make sure findings reach an owner and get closed.

- Secure an AI agent in production. Threat-model how our agent handles untrusted documents, emails and web content, and the tools and sandboxes it uses. Design defences against prompt injection and data exfiltration, and test them.

- Make security part of how we build. Review designs and changes that touch authentication, tenant isolation, secrets and data handling. Turn recurring findings into automated checks so the protection holds without depending on someone remembering.

- Respond to security incidents. Lead the technical response when something goes wrong: containment, investigation and the fix. Build the technical side of our breach playbooks with our information security lead, and run the review afterwards.

- Choose and run our security tooling. Evaluate and roll out a cloud security platform (such as Wiz) and the detection, alerting and logging we need across AWS and Azure. As our only product security specialist, use tooling and AI agents to cover more ground than one person could alone.

- Test our defences. Run red-team exercises, manage external penetration testers, and run breach drills with engineering so everyone knows their part before it matters.

- Close the loop on findings. Fix what penetration tests and security researchers report to us, run responsible disclosure, and keep the technical evidence for our SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls current, working with our information security lead.

- Make the work visible. Show leadership and engineering what the harness finds, what has been fixed and what risk remains, in plain language, with a recommendation for each open risk.

You should apply if you ✍️

- You build with agents. You'd rather put an agent loop on a problem than repeat a manual review. You've used AI agents to find, triage or fix security issues, and you aim for automation that leaves people to review only the exceptions.

- You have deep, hands-on security engineering experience. You've owned security for a cloud-native product or platform and can do the work yourself, from reading code and IAM policies to configuring detection and running an investigation.

- You know AWS security well. IAM, network design, KMS, GuardDuty, Security Hub, CloudTrail and how they fit together in a real production environment.

- You've led incident response. You've run a real security incident, including containment, investigation, communication and the follow-up, and you stay clear-headed under pressure.

- You take application and AI security seriously. You understand OWASP-class vulnerabilities, and you're interested in the new risks that come with LLM agents, such as prompt injection and over-broad tool access.

- You understand the product and the business. You know why a finding matters to our customers and our commercial position. You can tell a theoretical finding from one that puts customer data at risk, you spend effort where the risk is real, and you don't disappear down technical rabbit holes.

- You help teams ship safely. You find the secure way to do what the team needs, and you block work only when the risk justifies it. When you do, you explain why clearly enough that engineers understand and agree.

- You work independently. As our first in-house product security engineer, you'll set your own priorities, build the programme, and know when to bring in outside help.

- You bring people with you. You can explain a security risk to an engineer, a lawyer and a board member, adjusting the detail for each, and you change how teams work through influence rather than authority.

You'll most likely come from a security engineering, product security or application security role at a fast-growing startup, or from a security consultancy with hands-on delivery. We're open to different backgrounds if you can show the depth, judgement and automation-first approach this role needs.

It would also be nice if you have

- Experience securing LLM or agentic AI applications, or research into prompt injection and AI-specific threats.

- Harness engineering experience: building the tooling, evaluation loops and guardrails that let AI agents do real engineering work.

- Hands-on experience with SOC 2 and ISO 27001 audits.

- Experience with Azure, Kubernetes or container security, or sandboxed code execution.

- Familiarity with identity and SSO providers such as WorkOS or Okta.

- Experience in legal, financial or other regulated industries.

🔒 Security is everyone’s responsibility at Orbital. We ask all team members to follow our security policies, complete regular awareness training, and handle sensitive data with care in line with ISO 27001 standards. Spot something unusual? Reporting risks or incidents quickly helps us maintain the strong culture of security and compliance we all depend on.

💡 At Orbital, we’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We especially welcome applications from people who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. Even if you don’t meet every single requirement, or if the right role isn’t listed yet, we’d still love to hear from you.

You’ll play a key role in building out our digital assets platform, helping shape both the technology and engineering practices from the ground up. You’ll work side-by-side with traders and researchers, iterating quickly on ideas and translating market insights into production systems. From integrating with major centralised exchanges to improving system reliability in real-world conditions, your work will directly impact how we trade in this rapidly growing space.

What you’ll do 

- Design and build trading systems for digital asset markets

- Develop and manage connectivity to centralised exchanges such as Binance, Deribit, and OKX

- Work directly with traders and researchers to prototype and iterate on trading strategies

- Improve system reliability through automation, monitoring, and robust recovery mechanisms

- Troubleshoot issues across trading systems and exchange integrations

- Contribute to architecture and help shape the digital assets platform

- Take ownership of production systems and drive continuous improvements

Who you are 

- Experience building high-performance, reliable systems ideally involving exchange connectivity, market data, trading infrastructure or other real-time applications - experience with cryptocurrency exchanges, trading protocols or digital asset markets would be desirable. 

- A solid understanding of software architecture, networking, distributed systems and failure handling. 

- Beneficial to have C++ development skills, with experience building reliable production systems 

- Beneficial to have hands-on experience integrating with centralised cryptocurrency exchanges (e.g., Binance, Deribit, OKX)

- Beneficial to have experience working with cloud technologies (e.g., AWS, GCP, or similar)

- Strong problem-solving skills and an interest in tackling complex technical challenges in fast-paced environments

- A collaborative mindset with the ability to take ownership and partner closely with traders and researchers.

- Able to translate ambiguous trading requirements into practical engineering solutions

- Ownership-driven mindset with a focus on building resilient systems

Who we are 

At Optiver, our mission is to continuously improve the market. By providing liquidity and accurate pricing in various financial instruments, to multiple exchanges across the world, we participate in the safeguarding of healthy and efficient markets.

What you’ll get 

You’ll join a culture of collaboration and excellence, where you’ll be surrounded by curious thinkers and creative problem solvers. Motivated by a passion for continuous improvement, you’ll thrive in a supportive, high-performing environment alongside talented colleagues, working collectively to tackle the toughest problems in the financial markets.

In addition, you’ll receive:

- A performance-based bonus structure, enabling all of our employees to benefit from our global profit pool.

- 27 paid vacation days plus all UK public holidays.

- Daily breakfast and lunch, along with support on commuting expenses.

- Private medical insurance, pension scheme, and ClassPass fitness membership.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Core Video & Data
description:
At Hudl, we build great teams. We hire the best of the best to ensure you’re working with people you can constantly learn from. You’re trusted to get your work done your way while testing the limits of what’s possible and what’s next. We work hard to provide a culture where everyone feels supported, and our employees feel it—their votes helped us become one of the Top 100 Inspiring Workplaces .

We think of ourselves as the team behind the team, supporting the lifelong impact sports can have: the lessons in teamwork and dedication; the influence of inspiring coaches; and the opportunities to reach new heights. That’s why we help teams from all over the world see their game differently. Our products make it easier for coaches and athletes at any level to capture video, analyze data, share highlights and more.

Ready to join us?

Your Role

We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join our Core Data team in London.

This team builds the systems that power how Hudl understands sport at scale. From identifying players and teams across thousands of leagues to processing the moments that become highlights, stats and analysis, our services sit at the center of Hudl's platform.

As a Senior Engineer, you'll help shape the technical direction of the Global Sports Library (GSL), the backbone that connects identities, metadata and game context across Hudl products. You'll design and evolve APIs, distributed systems and large-scale data pipelines that ensure Hudl products operate from a consistent understanding of the game.

This role is deeply backend-focused and comes with significant ownership. You'll tackle complex engineering challenges around scalability, entity resolution, data consistency and platform architecture, while helping raise the technical bar across the team through design leadership, mentoring and pragmatic decision-making.

The systems you build won't support just one product or one sport. They'll become shared capabilities used across Hudl's ecosystem, powering experiences for teams, athletes and fans around the world.

- Be a key technical leader. You'll support the team by breaking down complex engineering problems, advocating for best practices and guiding others in addition to your focus on delivery.

- Maintain efficiency. You'll ensure your team delivers high-impact work efficiently by focusing on outcomes over outputs. Your leadership will empower the team to make data-driven decisions and iterate quickly on feedback.

- Collaborate across disciplines. You'll work closely with leaders from various disciplines to plan and deliver enhancements across our product suite. Your ability to integrate diverse perspectives will be key to driving innovation.

- Foster Agile practices. You'll participate actively in Scrum ceremonies and play a significant role in maintaining a strong team culture.

Location 

Time spent collaborating with your teammates in-office will be a regular part of how you work. We're currently considering applicants within commuting distance of London. You'll be expected to work more days in-office than remote, but will have the freedom to coordinate your specific in-office schedule with your team.

Must-Haves

- Strong technical proficiency. You have extensive experience in full-stack engineering and have spent time with cloud-based systems and services. You're also an advocate of TDD and CI/CD.

- Technical coaching experience. You're comfortable translating requirements, creating architectural proposals and guiding other engineers through implementation.

- A collaborative, team-first mindset. You know building excellent software is a team effort and you're willing to pitch in whenever a teammate needs a hand.

- Mentor mentality. You believe in the multiplier mindset and enjoy helping fellow engineers hone their skills through code reviews and pair programming.

Nice-to-Haves

- Tech stack knowledge. Professional background in C#, GraphQL, Elastic, MongoDB and AWS is ideal.

- Experience with media at scale. You've worked with video encoding and on-demand rendering in a professional setting.

- Passion for sports. You have an interest in the sports world and an understanding of sports analytics is a definite plus.

- Familiarity with hybrid teams. You've worked with hybrid or remote teams before and can adapt quickly to our working environment.

Our Role

- Champion work-life harmony. We'll give you the flexibility you need in your work life (e.g., flexible vacation time above any required statutory leave, company-wide holidays, remote work options and more) so you can enjoy your personal life too. Plus, every five years, we give you a paid sabbatical to unplug and recharge.

- Guarantee autonomy. We have an open, honest culture and we trust our people from day one. Your team will support you, but you'll own your work and have the agency to try new ideas.

- Encourage career growth. We're lifelong learners who encourage professional development. We'll give you tons of resources and opportunities to keep growing.

- Provide an environment to help you succeed. We've invested in our offices, designing incredible spaces with our employees in mind. But whether you're at the office or working remotely, we'll provide you the tech you need to do your best work.

- Support your wellbeing. Depending on location, we offer medical and retirement benefits for employees—but no matter where you're located, we have resources like our Employee Assistance Program and employee resource groups to support your mental health.

Compensation

The base salary range for this role is displayed below— starting salaries will typically fall near the middle of this range. 

We make compensation decisions based on an individual's experience, skills and education in line with our internal pay equity practices. 

This role will also be eligible for a long-term incentive (LTI) award. Any bonuses awarded are based on individual and company performance paid at Hudl's discretion.

£66,000 — £111,000 GBP

description:
Our Mission:

Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement.

Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Our AI-first platform changes that: our agents capture requests, route approvals, onboard suppliers, flag risk and track every renewal, while anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer grounded in their own company’s data. Buying becomes painless for everyone, procurement gets a seat at the table, and our customers have saved more than 100,000 hours of manual work so far.

Companies like Spotify, PayPal, T. Rowe Price, JustEat, Adyen and S&P Global run procurement on Omnea. We’re backed by $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners and Accel, and we’ve been named the UK’s number one startup in the Startups 100, ranked 11th on Sifted’s 2026 list of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, and recognised as one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies.

Talent density matters more to us than almost anything else. We keep the bar high in every team, so everyone here has real ownership and real impact. Our team is full of former founders and operators who’ve scaled unicorns, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside them.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here .

The Role

As Omnea's Account Manager, you own the relationship with our customers across their entire lifecycle, working with some of our largest and most strategic accounts. Your job is to make sure customers get real, measurable value from Omnea from day one, and to turn that value into renewals, expansion, and upsell.

Omnea's product is sticky: it's a business transformation, not a point tool, so once a customer is live, expansion tends to follow. Your focus skews heavily toward that expansion motion, not just keeping accounts renewed.

You'll build deep, long-term relationships with your champions and become a trusted advisor to stakeholders at every level, from procurement managers up to CFOs. You'll be the internal voice of the customer, working closely with both technical and commercial teams to keep Omnea customer-centric at its core.

This is an early hire on the customer team, working directly with Abs , Ben , and Rebe to build the function from the ground up. There's no fixed playbook yet: you'll help write it.

What You'll Do

- Own a revenue number: You'll carry an NRR quota covering both expansion and retention across your enterprise book. That means proactively identifying upsell opportunities, running commercial conversations at exec level, and owning the renewal process end-to-end.

- Build relationships that go all the way to the top: Your relationships will run from procurement managers to CFOs. You'll multi-thread across each account, building genuine trust across multiple stakeholders, and you'll be the person customers call when something goes wrong or when they're thinking about what's next.

- Build the playbook from scratch: There's no fully built playbook yet - you'll help shape it. You'll work alongside an exceptional implementation team, product experts, and leadership that have scaled world-class companies to define the commercial rhythms, norms, and processes to set the standard as the function grows.

- Shape what Omnea builds next: You're the closest person to what our customers will and won't pay for. You'll feed that signal directly to Product and Revenue leadership, surfacing what's blocking adoption, what's driving expansion, and where we should be investing.

What's Different About This Role

- This isn't a traditional post-sale account management role. Omnea's product is a business transformation, not a point tool, so most of your quota comes from expansion, not just renewal.

- We're not looking for a narrow "Account Manager" background. We want people from GTM roles broadly or from customer-facing roles with heavy commercial/GTM crossover.

- There's no fully built playbook. You'll define the commercial rhythms and processes as you go, working directly with Abs, Ben, and Rebe.

- You'll be as close to the product roadmap as anyone outside Product itself: what you hear from customers directly shapes what gets built next.

About You

We don't expect you to know exactly how to do all of this when you join. We're looking for someone with the right attitude and skillset to take this on.

TL;DR: you're commercially sharp, and you instinctively know how to navigate complex organisations. You might come from a GTM role (sales, customer success, partnerships) or a customer-facing role with heavy GTM crossover. What matters is that you've worked in real enterprise environments, managed senior stakeholders with high expectations, and have a track record of getting things done.
